added.title: Senior Machine Learning Engineer
added.description:
Job Description

Implements machine learning (ML) model serving for production. Ensures the readiness of machine learning models for deployment in production. Automates machine learning workflows. Creates infrastructure and frameworks to monitor the performance of machine learning models in deployment. Evaluates potential data quality, security, and/or privacy issues and their impacts on modeling. Provides troubleshooting and debugging support. Addresses issues in machine learning serving infrastructure and workflows. Collaborates with stakeholders to integrate machine learning models into new or extant systems. Develops, maintains, and refines tools, platforms, and services for internal use. Develops efficient, bug-free code from scratch. Maintains familiarity with current developments in the machine learning field and integrates knowledge into model development.

Responsibilities

Key Responsibilities

Machine Learning and Data Modeling – Model Productionization:

– Utilizes machine learning (ML) and software development knowledge to implement ML model serving for production.

– Collaborates with multiple stakeholders, such as Development Leads, Product Management, Operations, and Release Management, to make, adopt, and communicate technical decisions, and shape the development and delivery of software.

Model serving Development and Deployment – Model Deployment:

– Ensures ML model serving readiness for deployment by scaling models, cleaning model code, and ensuring production quality standards are met.

– Automates model serving workflows, from data extraction, transformation, and loading (ETL) to model deployment and monitoring, to establish the continuous integration and continuous delivery of machine learning solutions.

Model Development and Deployment – Model Serving Performance:

– Creates infrastructure and frameworks to monitor the performance and alignment with design criteria of trained models and/or systems.

– Proactively monitors the performance of deployed models and troubleshoots independently or in collaboration with Data Science.

– Develops novel metrics that provide analytical insights to non-technical stakeholders on how well machine learning models are operating.

Internal Collaborations and Impacts – Model Integration and Operation:

– Collaborates with multiple stakeholders (e.g., data scientists, software developers) to integrate open source models into new or existing systems.

– Understands operational considerations of model deployment (e.g., performance, scalability, stability, maintenance).

– Provides expert troubleshooting and debugging support, addresses issues in machine learning engineering infrastructure and workflow, and creates robust solutions to prevent future problems.

Internal Collaborations and Impacts – Tool Development:

– Develops, maintains, and refines tools, platforms, environments, and services for internal use.

Internal Collaborations and Impacts – Coding and Documentation:

– Develops efficient, bug-free, medium-complexity code from scratch, and properly maintains and organizes the existing codebase.

– Implements best practices for version control, code review, and code delivery/deployment.

– Builds and maintains professional documentation for technical processes (experimentation, data collection and analyses, model building).

– Tests and reviews code for bugs.

Machine Learning Engineering Expertise:

– Maintains familiarity with current developments in the machine learning engineering field and integrates knowledge into model development.

– Maintains familiarity with the usage and development of third-party machine learning frameworks, packages, and libraries (e.g., PyTorch, TensorFlow, Keras) to continuously evaluate their performance and scalability, and integrate them into production environments.

Core Responsibilities

Planning & Execution:

– Manages and coordinates moderately complex tasks, monitoring timelines and deliverables to ensure timely completion and adherence to requirements for a moderately sized project or initiative.

– Efficiently delegates, monitors, and prioritizes work across multiple projects, providing technical oversight and adjusting plans to address shifts in resources or timelines.

Collaboration & Partnership:

Responsibilities:

– Collaborates across the organization to align on expectations and achieve shared objectives.

– Leverages understanding of business leaders, stakeholders, and/or customers to ensure proposed solutions meet their needs.

– Supports inclusivity by actively seeking and listening to diverse perspectives, ensuring others feel heard and respected.

Problem Solving:

– Identifies and addresses moderately complex issues by analyzing a wide range of data and/or information to identify solutions in accordance with standard practices.

– Proactively escalates unresolved or critical issues with a thorough assessment and suggests potential solutions.

– Reviews, contributes to, and documents problem solving strategies.

Continuous Learning:

– Pursues learning opportunities to expand knowledge and skills and/or tools in new areas and stays abreast of the latest industry trends and best practices.

– Proactively seeks and leverages ongoing feedback and training to improve skills.

– Coaches and mentors junior team members, fostering continuous learning and knowledge sharing within and across teams.

Continuous Improvement:

– Develops ideas, recommends updates, and/or collaborates on the implementation of process improvements to increase the efficiency and effectiveness of processes, protocols, and workflows across teams, and evaluates the impact on key stakeholders.

– Solicits feedback from others on ideas for alternative approaches and methods for continued improvement.

Performance and Development:

– Contributes to the talent development pipeline by participating in candidate interviews, assessing candidates, and providing hiring recommendations.

added.title: Staff Software AI Engineer
added.description:
About Rivian

Rivian is on a mission to keep the world adventurous forever. This goes for the emissions-free Electric Adventure Vehicles we build, and the curious, courageous souls we seek to attract.

As a company, we constantly challenge what’s possible, never simply accepting what has always been done. We reframe old problems, seek new solutions and operate comfortably in areas that are unknown. Our backgrounds are diverse, but our team shares a love of the outdoors and a desire to protect it for future generations.

Role Summary

Rivian’s Applied AI team builds AI products that help engineers across the company design, build and support our vehicles. As a Staff AI Software Engineer specializing in agentic applications, you will shape the technical direction for how Rivian integrates AI into the way its people work. You will bring large language models together with enterprise knowledge and tools to build internal applications at scale, beginning with core product engineering workflows and expanding across the vehicle development lifecycle.

Your focus will be on automating complex workflows, accelerating decision-making and reducing manual effort. You will establish the architecture, engineering standards and evaluation practices needed to deliver reliable, scalable and observable AI applications, with measurable impact and capabilities that can be reused across the organization.

You will partner with Rivian’s product, systems and data teams while remaining hands-on in the design and implementation of the most critical components. This role will be located in Palo Alto, CA and report to our Sr. Manager, Applied AI for Product Engineering.

Responsibilities

Platform architecture. Define and own the agent platform architecture, including orchestration of long-running, multi-step agents, persistent state management, tool integration, permission-aware access to enterprise data, and evaluation infrastructure that gates production releases.
Technical direction. Establish reusable patterns, interfaces and engineering standards so that capabilities developed for one application can be adopted across the organization.
Production quality. Set the bar for reliability, observability and evaluation of AI systems. Ensure production applications meet defined quality, latency and cost targets against established baselines.
Hands-on engineering. Lead the design and implementation of the most complex components, deliver reference implementations, and resolve critical integration and reliability challenges.
Technology strategy. Evaluate emerging models, frameworks and tools; lead technical decisions on build versus buy and vendor selection; translate relevant advances into a roadmap with measurable impact.
Security and governance. Partner with Security, Legal and Compliance to embed authorization, auditability and data governance into the platform and its applications.
Talent development. Raise the engineering bar through design and code reviews, mentoring and participation in hiring.

Qualifications

8+ years of professional software engineering experience, including technical leadership of complex production systems.
Shipped and operated LLM-based or agentic applications with real users in production, with evidence of measured quality, adoption and business impact.
Deep understanding of agent system design: orchestration, tool calling, retrieval and grounding, context and memory management, durable execution, verification and evaluation of nondeterministic systems.
Expertise in backend and distributed systems: APIs, asynchronous execution, state management, fault tolerance and observability at scale.
Expert-level Python and experience deploying services on cloud infrastructure with containers and automated delivery pipelines.
A record of setting technical direction and engineering practices adopted beyond your own team, with demonstrable impact on the systems and engineers that depended on them.
Experience integrating with enterprise systems and data under security, privacy and permission constraints.
Ability to turn ambiguous user needs into practical technical solutions and to communicate clearly with engineers, domain experts and executives.
Bachelor’s, Master’s or Ph.D. in Computer Science, Engineering or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience with multi-agent systems that include verification or adversarial checking, persistent state, and recovery or human-approval mechanisms.
Experience with multimodal applications, document or engineering-drawing understanding, vision models or computer-use agents.
Familiarity with product development tooling: CAD, PLM, simulation or CAE, or physics-informed machine learning.
Experience improving AI systems through failure analysis, feedback loops, model adaptation or fine-tuning.
Experience building AI infrastructure or capabilities adopted by multiple teams, or forward-deployed experience at an AI lab or agent-infrastructure company.

Pay Disclosure

The salary range for this role is $206,500 - $258,100 for California based applicants. This is the lowest to highest salary we in good faith believe we would pay for this role at the time of this posting. An employee’s position within the salary range will be based on several factors including, but not limited to, specific competencies, relevant education, qualifications, certifications, experience, skills, geographic location, shift, and organizational needs.

The successful candidate may be eligible for annual performance bonus and equity awards.

We offer a comprehensive package of benefits for full-time and part-time employees, their spouse or domestic partner, and children up to age 26, including but not limited to paid vacation, paid sick leave, and a competitive portfolio of insurance benefits including life, medical, dental, vision, short-term disability insurance, and long-term disability insurance to eligible employees. You may also have the opportunity to participate in Rivian’s 401(k) Plan and Employee Stock Purchase Program if you meet certain eligibility requirements. Full-time employee coverage is effective on their first day of employment. Part-time employee coverage is effective the first of the month following 90 days of employment. More information about benefits is available at rivianbenefits.com.

You can apply for this role through careers.rivian.com (or through internal-careers-rivian.icims.com if you are a current employee). This job is not expected to be closed any sooner than 12/30/26

Equal Opportunity

Rivian is an equal opportunity employer and complies with all applicable federal, state, and local fair employment practices laws. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, national origin, ancestry, sex, sexual orientation, gender, gender expression, gender identity, genetic information or characteristics, physical or mental disability, marital/domestic partner status, age, military/veteran status, medical condition, or any other characteristic protected by law.

Rivian is committed to ensuring that our hiring process is accessible for persons with disabilities. If you have a disability or limitation, such as those covered by the Americans with Disabilities Act, that requires accommodations to assist you in the search and application process, please email us at candidateaccommodations@rivian.com.

Candidate Data Privacy and Technology

Rivian may collect, use and disclose your personal information or personal data (within the meaning of the applicable data protection laws) when you apply for employment and/or participate in our recruitment processes (“Candidate Personal Data”). This data includes contact, demographic, communications, educational, professional, employment, social media/website, network/device, recruiting system usage/interaction, security and preference information. Rivian may use your Candidate Personal Data for the purposes of (i) tracking interactions with our recruiting system; (ii) carrying out, analyzing and improving our application and recruitment process, including assessing you and your application and conducting employment, background and reference checks; (iii) establishing an employment relationship or entering into an employment contract with you; (iv) complying with our legal, regulatory and corporate governance obligations; (v) recordkeeping; (vi) ensuring network and information security and preventing fraud; and (vii) as otherwise required or permitted by applicable law.

Rivian may share your Candidate Personal Data with (i) internal personnel who have a need to know such information in order to perform their duties, including individuals on our People Team, Finance, Legal, and the team(s) with the position(s) for which you are applying; (ii) Rivian affiliates; and (iii) Rivian’s service providers, including providers of background checks, staffing services, and cloud services.

Rivian may transfer or store internationally your Candidate Personal Data, including to or in the United States, Canada, the United Kingdom, and the European Union and in the cloud, and this data may be subject to the laws and accessible to the courts, law enforcement and national security authorities of such jurisdictions.

How We Use AI in Our Hiring Process: To ensure transparency, we want candidates to know that Rivian uses iCIMS Talent Cloud Artificial Intelligence (TCAI) and AI-enabled tools to assist with screening, reviewing, organizing and highlighting profiles and applications that match the key requirements for each role.

AI does not make hiring decisions: Qualified candidate applications are reviewed by a member of our team, and all decisions throughout the process are made by humans. We use AI to support efficiency and consistency, not to replace human judgment. We are committed to a fair, thoughtful, and equitable experience for every candidate.

Participation in AI profile matching is entirely voluntary. If you prefer that your profile not be used in this process, you can opt out at any time. Opting out means your profile will be excluded from automated matching and will not be surfaced for additional roles through this system. Your current application remains active and will not be affected in any way.

Please note that we are currently not accepting applications from third party application services.

added.title: Staff Data Scientist, Credit Policy (Square Financial Services)
added.description:
Block builds simple, powerful tools that make progress towards an economy that’s truly open to all.

Each of our brands unlocks different aspects of the economy for more people. Square makes commerce and financial services accessible to sellers. Cash App is the easy way to spend, send, and store money. Afterpay is transforming the way customers manage their spending over time. TIDAL is a music platform that empowers artists to thrive as entrepreneurs. Bitkey is a simple self-custody wallet built for bitcoin. Proto is a suite of bitcoin mining products and services. Together, we’re helping build a financial system that is open to everyone. Join us.

The Role

The Credit and Lending team is responsible for the predictive intelligence that underpins Block’s primary capital-intensive products. These products unlock unique access to credit for our customers, many of whom are otherwise underbanked and underserved by the traditional financial system. As a member of the Credit Policy team within Square Financial Services (SFS), you will occupy a high-leverage role at the intersection of regulated banking and advanced autonomous systems. This position requires end-to-end ownership of credit policy, from the evaluation of novel data signals to the design of the decisioning logic that drives Block’s top-line growth. Beyond policy design, this role carries core responsibility for credit policy governance: ensuring that policy changes and experiments are rigorously designed, reviewed, documented, monitored, and reported in line with the expectations of a regulated bank.

Our credit products are material drivers of the company’s profitability and are frequently highlighted in executive reviews and quarterly earnings reports. We are seeking a scientifically-minded contributor capable of delivering extraordinary individual leverage to expand our underwriting capabilities into previously untapped segments through pragmatic policy evolution and advanced modeling techniques.

You Will

Apply a rigorous scientific mindset to the challenge of underwriting new customer segments, involving the evaluation of alternative external data sources and the design of new policy strategies to expand access while protecting the portfolio.
Own credit policy governance and reporting: maintain policy documentation, change logs, and approval artifacts, and deliver recurring portfolio performance and policy-impact reporting to credit risk committees, senior leadership, and bank oversight functions.
Propose and design experiments for credit products — champion/challenger tests, randomized holdouts, and staged rollouts across approval, limit, and pricing strategy — with clear hypotheses, success metrics, guardrails, and loss-exposure budgets.
Review experiment designs proposed by partner teams, assessing statistical rigor, sample sizing, risk exposure, fair lending considerations, and alignment with credit policy and regulatory requirements before launch.
Form policy guidelines and frameworks — risk appetite thresholds, approval and limit standards, and concentration limits — that enable credit portfolios to scale responsibly while meeting growth, loss, and profitability objectives.
Partner with Risk Management, Compliance and Internal Audit teams to ensure policy changes meet governance standards and are well documented and exam-ready.
Support team members in ad-hoc and scheduled updates to existing policies and strategies, and help troubleshoot issues in a real-time production environment.
Operate effectively within the framework of a regulated bank (SFS), balancing rapid innovation with the requirements of safety, soundness, and compliance.

Qualifications

8+ years of related experience with a Bachelor's degree; or 6+ years and a Master's degree; or a PhD with 3+ years experience; or equivalent experience
A degree in a technical field (e.g., Computer Science, Mathematics, Statistics, Physics, or Engineering). We have a strong preference for candidates with a demonstrated track record of scientific research or an advanced degree.
Demonstrated experience in credit policy governance at a bank, fintech, or consumer/small business lender — including documenting and approving policy changes, preparing materials for credit or risk committees, and supporting regulatory exams and internal audits.
Hands-on experience proposing, designing, and reviewing experiments for credit products (e.g., champion/challenger tests, randomized holdouts, and staged rollouts on approval, line assignment, or pricing), including power and sample sizing, loss-exposure guardrails, and decision-ready readouts.
A track record of building and owning portfolio monitoring and reporting — KPIs, early-warning indicators, vintage and roll-rate analysis — used to steer credit policy and communicate performance to leadership.
Experience translating business objectives into credit policy guidelines, such as risk appetite thresholds, approval and limit standards, and concentration limits, that allow portfolios to scale while staying within loss and profitability targets.
Familiarity with regulatory expectations for credit products is strongly preferred.
Strong quantitative intuition and data visualization skills, with a proven ability to conduct sophisticated ad-hoc and exploratory analysis.
Strong proficiency in SQL and Python preferred, including the ability to contribute across the analytical stack—from data pipelines to production-ready policy logic.
The versatility to communicate clearly with both technical and non-technical audiences, particularly in the context of high-visibility projects and senior stakeholders.
A pragmatic approach to problem-solving, with a willingness to utilize whichever tool is most appropriate for the situation while balancing complex business, technical, and regulatory constraints.

added.title: Senior Staff Data Scientist, Product Data Science (Mailchimp)
added.description:
Overview

The Mailchimp Product Data Science team turns product and customer data into insights and models that shape Mailchimp's product strategy. We work as thought partners with Product, Design, Engineering, Marketing, Finance, and Pricing to drive data-driven decisions through experimentation, causal measurement, and deep customer analytics.

We're looking for a Senior Staff Data Scientist to be an analytical leader for Mailchimp's product growth. In this high-impact individual contributor role, you'll set the measurement vision across the full customer journey: sign-up and onboarding, activation, conversion to paid, engagement, and long-term retention. The role raises the scientific bar for how we experiment and size opportunities, and it shapes product and business strategy at the senior leadership level. It's also hands-on, focused on the highest-leverage problems and on helping the team adopt AI-native workflows that let us move faster.

This role is based in New York, NY / Mountain View, CA / Atlanta, GA under Intuit's hybrid model, 3 days per week in office.

Responsibilities

Influence product strategy: Be a strategic thought partner to senior Product and business leaders. Shape Mailchimp's growth roadmap with deep dives into customer segmentation, onboarding and activation funnels, feature adoption, pricing and packaging, and retention.
Set the analytics vision: Own the measurement framework, north-star and guardrail metrics, and leading indicators for the self-serve customer journey, from free and trial sign-ups to paid conversion, bookings, and recurring revenue.
Lead experimentation and causal measurement: Drive a culture of rigorous, iterative experimentation. Design complex tests (A/B/n, sequential, holdouts, long-running), apply Bayesian and frequentist inference, and use causal inference methods such as difference-in-differences, propensity score matching, and synthetic control where randomized tests aren't possible.
Size and prioritize opportunities: Build opportunity-sizing and forecasting frameworks that turn product initiatives into incremental revenue impact, accounting for retention curves and the winner's curse, so leadership can prioritize investment.
Uncover growth opportunities: Use first-principles thinking and exploratory analysis to find untapped levers across the funnel, including in-product onboarding, lifecycle marketing, paid media, and plan upgrades.
Shape the AI-native roadmap: Partner with Product and Engineering to measure AI-powered features in Mailchimp. Build ML and LLM-based solutions such as propensity models, personalization, and automated insights for hard product problems.
Raise the scientific bar: Build reusable analytical frameworks, governed metric definitions, and self-serve tools that improve decision-making at scale. Champion strong instrumentation and data quality.
Lead and mentor: Be a technical lead for the Product Data Science team. Coach and grow senior and staff data scientists, review their methods, and model executive-ready storytelling.

8+ years in data science, product analytics, or a related field, with a proven record of driving product strategy and measurable business impact.
Experience in B2B SaaS, subscription, or freemium/self-serve businesses strongly preferred. Familiarity with marketing technology or small-business customers is a plus.
Expert SQL and data modeling skills on cloud data warehouses (BigQuery preferred), plus advanced Python or R.
Deep expertise in experimental design and causal inference, with the judgment to balance statistical rigor against speed of decision-making.
Track record of sizing opportunities and forecasting revenue impact, including funnel, cohort, and retention analysis.
Hands-on experience applying machine learning (classification, regression, uplift or propensity modeling) and LLM/GenAI workflows to real product problems.
Proficient in an AI-native data science tech stack (for example, Claude, Cursor, or Codex with MCPs, CLIs, and APIs) and eager to keep building how the team works with AI.
Excellent executive communication. You turn complex analysis into clear narratives and recommendations, and you've influenced senior leaders across Product, Marketing, and Finance.
Experience leading ambiguous, cross-functional work where the question, metric definitions, or methodology have to be set before the analysis can start.
Demonstrated mentorship and technical leadership of other data scientists.
Bachelor's or graduate degree in a quantitative field such as Statistics, Economics, Computer Science, Mathematics, or Operations Research, or equivalent practical experience.

added.title: Forward Deployed Engineer
added.description:
About Sentry

Software runs the world and the pace is faster than ever. Sentry helps developers fix errors and performance issues before users notice, so teams can spend less time firefighting and more time building.

Trusted by 200,000+ organizations, Sentry is today’s application monitoring standard and our team is building its AI-native future.

About The Role

Forward Deployed Engineers at Sentry help our largest customers get real value from Sentry, from integrating the SDK to making sure the right alerts and issues reach the right people at the right time. This role is a Senior Solutions Engineer who goes further: you'll help us build Sentry's forward deployed motion.

That means working shoulder to shoulder with our most important customers, often inside their codebases and workflows, instead of advising from the outside. When a customer's problem needs more than a best-practices doc, such as a custom integration, a tricky instrumentation setup, or a working prototype, you'll build it with them, then turn what you learn into repeatable patterns for the rest of the team.

Forward deployed work is new here and you will have a part in building this arm. You'll start with the core Solutions Engineering work and take on more hands-on deployment work as customers pull you into it, helping define what this motion looks like at Sentry. The goal is simple: reduce time to value. The outcomes we care about:

Developers can quickly find and resolve slowdowns and errors in their applications.
Customers get to value faster, and the lessons from each deployment make the product better for everyone.

In this role you will

Turn customer goals into a plan. Understand customers' pain points and objectives, then act as their trusted advisor, translating them into implementation plans, workshops, and best practices that show clear business value.
Get Sentry set up, in the code. With the customer's permission, work in their codebase like a member of their engineering team, delivering the pull requests that fully set up Sentry so data is flowing from day one.
Instrument what matters most. Add custom telemetry for a customer's most critical user journeys and build the dashboards and alerts that go with it.
Lead migrations. Move customers off their existing observability tools by setting up their Sentry organization and delivering PRs that introduce Sentry and remove the old solution.
Work like a trusted contractor. Stay within the scope and access you've been given, take extra care in live environments, test thoroughly, and ship pull requests that customer engineers are glad to merge. Embed with their teams, including on site, when it helps.
Build the motion. Turn one-off deployments into repeatable playbooks and tooling, help define how forward deployed engagements are scoped and measured, and bring what you learn back to Product and Engineering.

You’ll love this job if you

You'd rather sit with a customer's engineers and fix the problem in their code than write them a recommendation
Enjoy talking about technology and interfacing with engineers and engineering leaders.
Appreciate working in a dynamic environment, on a variety of projects with customers from lots of different industries.
Love flexing your creative brain by developing solutions, resources, and content from scratch (scripts, code samples, demos, sales-consumable collateral/documents, etc.).
Have a fast-paced, results-driven mindset.
Love developer tools, open-source, and/or all things software development life cycle!

Qualifications

3+ years of experience, with some mixture being Software Engineering and Solutions Engineering/Implementation and at least 1+ year being a FDE
Hands-on experience working with programming languages and frameworks including JavaScript, Python, Node.js, Java, PHP, .NET, Ruby, React, React Native, Mobile Native (iOS and/or Android), etc
Excellent communication and presentation skills, with credibility in front of engineers and engineering leaders
Problem solver, knowledgable, and can-doer
Bonus: experience with observability, APM, or error monitoring tools, including migrating customers from another vendor, or helping build a forward deployed or customer engineering function

A successful candidate’s actual base salary (or hourly wage) amount will be determined by a variety of relevant factors including, without limitation, the candidate’s work location, education, work and other relevant experience, skills, and job-related knowledge. A successful candidate will be eligible to participate in Sentry’s employee benefit plans/programs applicable to the candidate’s position (including incentive compensation, equity grants, paid time off, and group health insurance coverage). added.title: Research Scientist II, Battery
added.description:
Description

Do you want to shape the battery energy storage technology at Amazon? We are looking for a Research Scientist to drive the technical evaluation of battery energy storage technology, from cells today to modules, systems and the technologies around them as our scope grows, and to be the technical interface with the suppliers and partners who work with us.

You will conduct technical evaluations from test design through data analysis: help identify candidate technologies and supplies, engage their engineering teams, design test plans and protocol, coordinate sample sourcing and testing, and turn results into clear technical recommendations.

You will visit supplier factories and laboratories, and you will work closely with your manager and colleagues across engineering, procurement, and business development, giving you direct exposure to how technical judgements become business decisions. This role suits someone who enjoys deep technical work and wants to grow into broader cross-functional influence.

Key job responsibilities

Conduct technical evaluations of battery energy storage technologies, starting with lithium-ion cells and extending to modules, systems and related components: review specifications, test reports, safety certifications and manufacturing quality data, and identify gaps and risks.
Design test plans and protocols covering performance, cycle and calendar ageing, thermal characterisation and abuse/safety testing; propose acceptance criteria; and execute test programs under direction of Senior Scientist.
Coordinate the technical aspects of sample sourcing (specifications, shipping, storage, data management), partnering with Legal and Procurement through your manager
Process and analyse test data (capacity fade, resistance growth, efficiency, thermal behaviour) and build repeatable analysis pipelines and lifetime models.
Support supplier and partner engagements by contributing technical expertise in deep-dive sessions, factory visits, and quality assessments.
Prepare technical assessments, analysis summaries, and draft recommendations that feed into leadership reviews. Work with cross-functional colleagues, primarily in engineering and procurement, to move evaluations from technical findings toward decisions.
Travel frequently, domestically and internationally, for supplier and partner visits.

A day in the life

Your week mixes deep technical work with collaboration and learning. One day you might be reviewing a supplier's test data and specifications, turning an open question into a change to a running test plan. The next, you could be joining a technical deep-dive with a manufacturer's engineering team, or preparing observations and diligence items ahead of a factory visit. You will work closely with the laboratory on incoming results, support your manager on coordination with Legal and Procurement for agreements and samples, and partner with engineering colleagues to explore what the findings mean for system design. You will regularly prepare technical summaries and draft recommendations that feed into leadership discussions, and from time to time you will present your own analysis directly. Several times a year you will travel to a factory or laboratory in North America, Europe, or Asia.

About The Team

We are a new team dedicated to Amazon's energy storage strategy. Our job is to give Amazon an independent, evidence-based view of energy storage technology: which cells and systems to trust, how long they will last, how they will fail and what they will cost. We work with suppliers and partners around the world and with colleagues across engineering, procurement, legal, finance and business development.

The team is at an early stage and its scope is growing quickly, from cells today to modules, systems and the technologies around them. You will be an early hire, so you will help shape how we evaluate technology, how we engage suppliers and how we present results, with a direct line of sight to the decisions your work informs. For the right person this is a role with high growth potential and a wide range of opportunities as the team expands.

Basic Qualifications

PhD, or Master's degree and 4+ years of quantitative field research experience
Experience investigating the feasibility of applying scientific principles and concepts to business problems and products
Experience analyzing both experimental and observational data sets

Preferred Qualifications

Knowledge of R, MATLAB, Python or similar scripting language
Experience with agile development
Experience building web based dashboards using common frameworks

added.title: Early Math, Research Scientist II
added.description:
About WestEd

As a community of over 1,000 researchers, practitioners, consultants, and administrative professionals from all backgrounds and life experiences, we are committed to making a qualitative difference in the lives of youth, children, and adults. We conduct and apply research, develop evidence-based solutions, and provide consulting services across the country in both rural and urban communities to improve equitable outcomes for individuals from infancy through adulthood. Serving as trusted partners in the areas of education, health, and justice, our teams enhance capacity within communities and school districts to prioritize impact — asking the right questions, customizing methodologies, developing relevant tools, and implementing best practices specific to a diverse range of stakeholder needs.

WestEd supports individual initiative, excellence, and hard work of all individuals in our hiring and work practices. WestEd complies with all applicable federal and state anti-discrimination laws, as well as OFCCP requirements. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to disability, or status as a protected veteran.

SPECIAL NOTICE REGARDING THE WORK LOCATION OF THIS POSITION—Although WestEd provides the option of working at one of its facilities for employees, many roles allow employees to choose to work remotely for their own convenience. The decision to allow remote work at the employee's convenience is based on the requirements of the position or project in question.

Brief Description

WestEd is seeking a Research Scientist II to lead mid- to large-sized or moderately complex research and evaluation projects, or components of larger projects, that generate credible, actionable evidence for the clients, partners, and communities we serve. You will oversee complex, multi-method studies, manage multiple concurrent work streams, and represent WestEd through presentations and publications at regional and national levels. You will also lead small to mid-sized proposals, build a pipeline of work, and mentor colleagues.

The Opportunity

WestEd's research and evaluation staff design, conduct, and share studies that give clients, partners, and communities evidence they can trust and use. As a Research Scientist II, you will help shape that work across the full study lifecycle, from design and data collection through analysis and dissemination, holding to high standards of methodological rigor, ethical integrity, and transparency.

You will lead mid- to large-sized or moderately complex projects, or major components of larger ones, and balance client needs, staff capacity, and project goals across multiple concurrent workstreams. You will contribute to project conceptualization and design, build trusted relationships with clients, partners, and funders, and extend WestEd's visibility through presentations and publications. You will also lead small to mid-sized proposals, build a pipeline of future work, and help your colleagues grow.

This position is also designed to expand our early childhood early mathematics work. You will help build that portfolio through partnerships, funding, and proposals. Initially, you will contribute to a 1.5-year grant project focused starting in January 2027 and concluding in June 2028. The continuation of this position beyond this grant is highly desired and contingent on funding renewal and performance.

Core Focus Areas And Responsibilities

Research and Methodologival Rigor

Oversee complex, multi-method studies and set quality assurance expectations across workstreams.
Guide methodological decisions, integrate approaches to meet project needs, and contribute to project conceptualization, design, and implementation.
Apply advances in data collection and analysis methods to proposals and project implementation, looking for cost efficiency and methodological precision that increase project impact.
Understand risk based on study design and proactively comply with WestEd policies and legal guidelines from the Legal Office, Office of Research Integrity, and Data Protection Office, guiding teams through any issues that arise.
Plan for possible anomalies in study implementation, data handling, and Institutional Review Board concerns, and communicate and document decisions to support team understanding.

Knowledge Translation and Influence

Synthesize findings across studies or work streams, drawing on deeper subject matter expertise and connecting to other bodies of evidence to identify cross-cutting themes and implications.
Author papers, briefs, and presentations that advance WestEd's reputation.
Represent WestEd through presentations, publications, and professional engagement at regional and national levels.
Coach others in structuring arguments, clarifying findings, and using evidence effectively.
Review and strengthen the writing of others, ensuring clarity, rigor, and coherence.

Project and Client Management

Lead mid-size to large or moderately complex projects, or components of larger projects, to ensure client satisfaction.
Manage multiple concurrent workstreams, ensuring integration and quality across staff and subcontractors while balancing client needs, staff capacity, and project goals.
Manage complex client relationships independently, aligning project strategy with client needs while safeguarding feasibility and rigor.
Anticipate risks and proactively guide clients through decisions that affect timeline, scope, or methodological approach.
Use data to demonstrate impact to clients and funders.

Business and Partnership Development

Lead full proposal development for small to mid-sized projects, or contribute substantially to large, complex proposals, in alignment with standards for high-quality proposals.
Model effective use of WestEd systems and processes for business and partnership development.
Scan the landscape for new opportunities and cultivate relationships with existing and prospective clients and partners to understand needs and shape ideas.
Engage with clients between projects to strengthen trust and build a pipeline of work.

What We're Looking For

Experience and Qualifications, Required

Ph.D. in child development, education, psychology or a related research field.
Deep knowledge of early mathematics development, early childhood education practices, and the policies and systems that shape early childhood education.
At least 5 years of experience leading applied research or evaluation studies, including mid- to large-sized or moderately complex projects with multiple concurrent workstreams.
Experience leading or contributing substantially to research or evaluation proposals and building relationships with clients, partners, and funders; Experience building a pipeline of work with existing and prospective clients and partners.
Record of presentations, publications, or other professional engagement at regional and national levels.
Commitment to centering the voices and priorities of the communities our work serves.
Expertise designing and overseeing complex, multi-method studies, including data collection and analysis.
Proficiency with statistical or analytic software (e.g., Stata, SPSS, R).
Knowledge of research ethics and compliance requirements, including Institutional Review Board processes and data security.
Ability to manage multiple concurrent workstreams, timelines, and staff while meeting client needs.
Strong written and oral communication skills for reports, presentations, and publications for diverse audiences.
Ability to mentor colleagues and provide clear direction and constructive feedback.

Preferred

At least five years of experience developing and leading early mathematics content that builds the capacity of ECE workforce and families to support children’s mathematics learning from birth through age eight.
Bilingual and biliterate English/Spanish.
Experience applying new and emerging methodological approaches to study design.
Experience coaching others in writing and presenting evidence effectively.

How You'll Approach The Work

Provides clear direction and feedback to project team members, sets expectations, monitors progress, and supports skill development through assignments.
Creates an inclusive team environment, models effective collaboration and communication, and mentors colleagues in technical and project management skills.
Integrates diverse perspectives to address complex issues, balances proven methods with innovative approaches, and anticipates risks and adjusts strategy proactively.
Develops a deep understanding of what matters to clients, partners, end users, and affected communities, including unstated needs, and designs solutions that address root causes.
Takes ownership of outcomes and results, not just tasks, and maintains high standards of quality, ethics, and transparency under pressure, addressing performance gaps constructively.
Resolves conflicts constructively, integrates input across workstreams, ensures clear communication within project teams, and coaches others in inclusive, generous collaboration.
Coaches others through change, builds practices that support team resilience and well-being, and creates psychologically safe environments where people learn from setbacks.

Location and Work Arrangement

Location/geography: West Coast, Pacific Southwest preferred
Work arrangement: Remote
Travel: This position travels for project-related work (e.g., in-person data collection, site visits, filming), WestEd offices (for meetings, professional learning, or other gatherings), client meetings, or conferences on an as-needed basis; estimated travel up to 20%.
Note: Visa sponsorship is not available for this position. Successful candidates must be authorized to work in the United States.

WestEd conducts a criminal background check, fingerprint validation and education verification for all new hires. Any offers of employment will be contingent on receiving a clear background check in accordance with applicable law.

The typical hiring range for this role is $122,400 to $153,000. The actual offer takes into account multiple factors, including but not limited to education, experience, internal equity, and other organizational needs.

15% contribution toward retirement effective day 1 of employment and immediately 100% vested

Life Insurance: value of 3x gross salary, max of 500k
Opportunities for annual merit-based performance increases + annual incentives
Professional development opportunities & mentorship program

Description

The Amazon Web Services Professional Services (ProServe) team is seeking a skilled Machine Learning Engineer to join our team at Amazon Web Services (AWS). Are you looking to work at the forefront of Machine Learning and AI? Would you be excited to apply Generative AI algorithms to solve real world problems with significant impact? In this role, you'll work directly with customers to design, evangelize, implement, and scale AI/ML solutions that meet their technical requirements and business objectives. You'll be a key player in driving customer success through their AI transformation journey, providing deep expertise in machine learning, generative AI, and best practices throughout the project lifecycle.

As a Machine Learning Engineer within the AWS Professional Services organization, you will be proficient in architecting complex, scalable, and secure machine learning solutions tailored to meet the specific needs of each customer. You'll help customers imagine and scope the use cases that will create the greatest value for their businesses, select and train and fine tune the right models, and define paths to navigate technical or business challenges. Working closely with stakeholders, you'll assess current data infrastructure, develop proof-of-concepts, and propose effective strategies for implementing AI and generative AI solutions at scale. You will design and run experiments, research new algorithms, and find new ways of optimizing risk, profitability, and customer experience.

The AWS Professional Services organization is a global team of experts that help customers realize their desired business outcomes when using the AWS Cloud. We work together with customer teams and the AWS Partner Network (APN) to execute enterprise cloud computing initiatives. Our team provides a collection of offerings which help customers achieve specific outcomes related to enterprise cloud adoption. We also deliver focused guidance through our global specialty practices, which cover a variety of solutions, technologies, and industries.

This position requires that the candidate selected be a US Citizen and must currently possess and maintain an active TS/SCI security clearance.

Key job responsibilities

Designing and implementing complex, scalable, and secure AI/ML solutions on AWS tailored to customer needs, including selecting and fine-tuning appropriate models for specific use cases

Developing and deploying machine learning models and generative AI applications that solve real-world business problems, conducting experiments and optimizing for performance at scale

Collaborating with customer stakeholders to identify high-value AI/ML use cases, gather requirements, and propose effective strategies for implementing machine learning and generative AI solutions

Providing technical guidance on applying AI, machine learning, and generative AI responsibly and cost-efficiently, troubleshooting throughout project delivery and ensuring adherence to best practices

Acting as a trusted advisor to customers on the latest advancements in AI/ML, emerging technologies, and innovative approaches to leveraging diverse data sources for maximum business impact

Sharing knowledge within the organization through mentoring, training, creating reusable AI/ML artifacts, and working with team members to prototype new technologies and evaluate technical feasibility

About The Team

Job Description

Implements machine learning (ML) model serving for production. Ensures the readiness of machine learning models for deployment in production. Automates machine learning workflows. Creates infrastructure and frameworks to monitor the performance of machine learning models in deployment. Evaluates potential data quality, security, and/or privacy issues and their impacts on modeling. Provides troubleshooting and debugging support. Addresses issues in machine learning serving infrastructure and workflows. Collaborates with stakeholders to integrate machine learning models into new or extant systems. Develops, maintains, and refines tools, platforms, and services for internal use. Develops efficient, bug-free code from scratch. Maintains familiarity with current developments in the machine learning field and integrates knowledge into model development.

Responsibilities

Key Responsibilities

Machine Learning and Data Modeling – Model Productionization:

– Utilizes machine learning (ML) and software development knowledge to implement ML model serving for production.

– Collaborates with multiple stakeholders, such as Development Leads, Product Management, Operations, and Release Management, to make, adopt, and communicate technical decisions, and shape the development and delivery of software.

Model serving Development and Deployment – Model Deployment:

– Ensures ML model serving readiness for deployment by scaling models, cleaning model code, and ensuring production quality standards are met.

– Automates model serving workflows, from data extraction, transformation, and loading (ETL) to model deployment and monitoring, to establish the continuous integration and continuous delivery of machine learning solutions.

Model Development and Deployment – Model Serving Performance:

– Creates infrastructure and frameworks to monitor the performance and alignment with design criteria of trained models and/or systems.

– Proactively monitors the performance of deployed models and troubleshoots independently or in collaboration with Data Science.

– Develops novel metrics that provide analytical insights to non-technical stakeholders on how well machine learning models are operating.

Internal Collaborations and Impacts – Model Integration and Operation:

– Collaborates with multiple stakeholders (e.g., data scientists, software developers) to integrate open source models into new or existing systems.

– Understands operational considerations of model deployment (e.g., performance, scalability, stability, maintenance).

– Provides expert troubleshooting and debugging support, addresses issues in machine learning engineering infrastructure and workflow, and creates robust solutions to prevent future problems.

Internal Collaborations and Impacts – Tool Development:

– Develops, maintains, and refines tools, platforms, environments, and services for internal use.

Internal Collaborations and Impacts – Coding and Documentation:

– Develops efficient, bug-free, medium-complexity code from scratch, and properly maintains and organizes the existing codebase.

– Implements best practices for version control, code review, and code delivery/deployment.

– Builds and maintains professional documentation for technical processes (experimentation, data collection and analyses, model building).

– Tests and reviews code for bugs.

Machine Learning Engineering Expertise:

– Maintains familiarity with current developments in the machine learning engineering field and integrates knowledge into model development.

– Maintains familiarity with the usage and development of third-party machine learning frameworks, packages, and libraries (e.g., PyTorch, TensorFlow, Keras) to continuously evaluate their performance and scalability, and integrate them into production environments.

Core Responsibilities

Planning & Execution:

– Manages and coordinates moderately complex tasks, monitoring timelines and deliverables to ensure timely completion and adherence to requirements for a moderately sized project or initiative.

– Efficiently delegates, monitors, and prioritizes work across multiple projects, providing technical oversight and adjusting plans to address shifts in resources or timelines.

Responsibilities:

– Collaborates across the organization to align on expectations and achieve shared objectives.

– Leverages understanding of business leaders, stakeholders, and/or customers to ensure proposed solutions meet their needs.

– Supports inclusivity by actively seeking and listening to diverse perspectives, ensuring others feel heard and respected.

Problem Solving:

– Identifies and addresses moderately complex issues by analyzing a wide range of data and/or information to identify solutions in accordance with standard practices.

– Proactively escalates unresolved or critical issues with a thorough assessment and suggests potential solutions.

– Reviews, contributes to, and documents problem solving strategies.

Continuous Learning:

– Pursues learning opportunities to expand knowledge and skills and/or tools in new areas and stays abreast of the latest industry trends and best practices.

– Proactively seeks and leverages ongoing feedback and training to improve skills.

– Coaches and mentors junior team members, fostering continuous learning and knowledge sharing within and across teams.

Continuous Improvement:

– Develops ideas, recommends updates, and/or collaborates on the implementation of process improvements to increase the efficiency and effectiveness of processes, protocols, and workflows across teams, and evaluates the impact on key stakeholders.

– Solicits feedback from others on ideas for alternative approaches and methods for continued improvement.

BMO is hiring a Senior AI Engineer to design, build and run production-grade AI solutions across Finance. You will own solutions end to end:

user experience and APIs
agentic workflows
retrieval and data integration
evaluation and ongoing monitoring

You will build on BMO's enterprise AI platform and within the Finance AI Governance Program. Your work will be safe and auditable, and it will hold up to regulatory review.

You will partner directly with leaders in FP&A, Controllership, Treasury and Finance Operations. Typical use cases include:

variance analysis and commentary
reconciliations and manual journal entries
close acceleration
controllership and policy research
treasury forecasting

This role is for engineers who have shipped AI to production, not only built prototypes.

Why join:

Shape how AI changes Finance at one of North America's largest banks, working with senior Finance leadership.
Build real solutions that go to production, on an enterprise AI platform designed for scale and governance.
Help set engineering and Responsible AI standards for the Finance AI function.

Key accountabilities

Solution engineering

Design, build and deploy end-to-end AI applications: web front ends (React/TypeScript), backend services and APIs (Python/FastAPI), and integration with Finance data and systems.
Translate Finance business problems into technical designs, and make sound trade-offs between accuracy, latency, cost and maintainability.

Agentic AI and LLM systems

Build multi-step agentic workflows using tool and function calling, MCP integrations, and orchestration frameworks.
Design retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) over Finance policies, documents and structured data, including chunking, embeddings, vector search and context engineering.
Embed human-in-the-loop controls for material judgments, approvals and financial postings.

Evaluation and quality

Build evaluation harnesses with golden datasets to measure accuracy, consistency, groundedness and regression across model and prompt changes.
Document methodology, assumptions and limitations. Define acceptance thresholds with business owners.

Production readiness and operations

Partner with the Technology and AI Platform teams on CI/CD, security reviews, resilience and support handover.
Use the shared enterprise platform services (AI gateway, guardrails, registry, observability) rather than building parallel tooling.
Instrument tracing, usage, cost and drift monitoring. Respond to and resolve production issues.

Governance, risk and data controls

Act as the AI Developer under the Risk and Finance AI Governance Program: complete use case documentation, testing evidence and Ongoing Monitoring Plans address conditions raised in Second Line reviews
Apply data classification, access controls, PII protection and lineage, in line with the Data Risk Directive, RDARR principles and model risk expectations.

Adoption and leadership

Run demos and pilots, gather feedback, and track adoption and value-realization metrics.
Build reusable patterns, components and templates that speed up future Finance AI use cases.
Review code, set engineering standards, and mentor analysts and junior engineers.

Qualifications

Required

7+ years of professional software engineering experience, including 2+ years building and deploying LLM or generative AI applications to production.
Expert Python, plus proficiency in a modern front-end framework (React/TypeScript preferred).
Strong API design, SQL and data modeling skills.
Hands-on experience with: agent orchestration frameworks (e.g., LangGraph, Semantic Kernel, AutoGen or equivalent) RAG architectures and vector databases prompt and context engineering
Experience with cloud AI services (Azure OpenAI / Azure AI Foundry and/or AWS Bedrock), containers, CI/CD and observability tooling.
Proven ability to evaluate non-deterministic systems and build automated test and evaluation pipelines.
Experience in a regulated environment, with an understanding of auditability, explainability, security and data privacy.
Ability to communicate technical concepts clearly to non-technical Finance stakeholders and senior leaders.
Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Mathematics or a related field, or equivalent experience.

Preferred

Finance domain knowledge: financial close, reconciliations, FP&A, treasury, liquidity or IRRBB.
Familiarity with model risk management guidance (e.g., OSFI E-23, SR 11-7).
Experience with Databricks, Snowflake or Power BI, and with Finance systems such as Oracle or Hyperion.
Experience building MCP servers or enterprise tool integrations for agents.
Experience using AI-assisted development tools (e.g., GitHub Copilot) within a governed engineering workflow.
Bilingual English/French is an asset.

Researches, builds, and implements scalable artificial intelligence systems capable of learning and making predictions to business requirements. Enhances data pipelines and lakes to ensure data is clean, accurate, and optimized for machine learning models. Monitors, evaluates, and optimizes learning processes to continuously improve high-performance models. Works with other data and analytics professionals to optimize, refine, automate and scale analysis into repeatable analytics solutions and decision support tools.

Designs and develops machine learning (ML) and deep learning systems.

Who We Are

Persona AI is building humanoid robots for the most demanding environments in heavy industry — shipyards, steel mills, fabrication facilities, and offshore platforms — performing welding, grinding, maintenance, inspection, and material-handling work that is dangerous, physically demanding, and increasingly difficult to staff.

We are backed by leading strategic and financial investors and engaged with global industrial leaders across Korea, Japan, the United States, and Singapore. Korea is the center of gravity for our early commercial strategy, anchored by relationships with the world’s leading shipbuilders and steelmakers. Our work spans both the robot platform itself and the systems, partners, and playbooks required to deploy it at scale.

Why Join Persona AI?

We offer competitive compensation, a performance-based bonus, 100% employer covered medical benefits for most healthcare plans, early-stage equity, competitive PTO, and company-wide paid winter break between December 24th and January 2nd.
You’ll shape technology that’s redefining the possibilities of robotics and human interaction.
Work alongside passionate teammates who value creativity, and continuous learning.

About The Role

We're looking for a Staff Deep Learning, Robot Manipulation Engineer
to help build and execute Persona AI's robot learning capability and roadmap. We're looking for exceptional talent who dream big, thrive on challenges, and love seeing their efforts make an impact on Persona’s humanoid robots doing real work in real-world environments.

You will drive and implement Persona’s learning-based manipulation direction, research and establish the best learning formula for Persona’s humanoid use cases such as welding and grinding, and continuously improve the robot fleet’s performance to achieve industrial-level robustness.

If you want to push the boundary of humanoid robot capability performing real-world tasks, this role is for you.

What You Will Be Doing

Design and implement advanced robot learning models and training procedures to achieve dexterous manipulation for humanoid robots with high DOF and multi-fingered hands.
Own the ML manipulation pipeline and roadmap, combining different learning paradigms to achieve real-world, industrial-level robustness.
Work with the Teleoperation and Data team to design data collection, sensor modularity, and data mixture strategies.
Leverage existing state-of-the-art manipulation models and contribute to the development of new architectures for emerging complex tasks.
Deploy trained manipulation models to robotic hardware, ensuring real-time performance, safety, and integration with control systems and sensors.
Keep up to date with the state of the art in ML research and development.
Develop and execute evaluation pipelines to rigorously test learned manipulation models, including real-world trials and simulation, measuring performance, robustness, and generalization across tasks and environments.
Collaborate in attracting, nurturing, and growing the machine learning team.

What We Are Looking For

5+ years of experience applying deep learning techniques to robotic manipulation in industrial settings.
Master's or PhD in Robotics, Computer Science, or a related field.
Courage and grit to tackle some of the most challenging problems in robot manipulation.
Strong understanding and proficiency with state-of-the-art algorithms and best practices in behavior cloning, reinforcement learning, vision-language-action models, foundation models, etc.
Experience with cloud computing and large-scale datasets.
Capable of writing high-quality software in Python, C++, or Rust.

Bonus Skills

Experience with other aspects of ML applied to robotics, including robot simulation, locomotion, computer vision, robot hardware, and sensors.
Published papers at top ML/Robotics conferences (ICML, ICRA, CoRL, RSS, NeurIPS, etc.).
Have trained models and deployed them to robots in production environments.

Strong Python and React engineering is the foundation—if you also bring experience in search systems, vector databases, or Elasticsearch, you'll hit the ground running from day one.

Build & Ship Search and AI-Powered Systems

Design, develop, and deploy production Python services end-to-end—from retrieval and ranking pipelines through client-facing APIs.
Build and integrate ML inference pipelines: embedding models, transformer-based classifiers, LLM-powered query understanding, and reranking services.
Develop event-driven, real-time architectures using GCP services—Cloud Run, Pub/Sub, GKE, Cloud Functions.
Write clean, well-tested, observable Python backends; own your services through deployment, monitoring, and on-call
Drive frontend architecture decisions, establishing development standards, and creating reusable component libraries.

Contribute to Search Infrastructure

Work alongside the Search Architect and ML Architect to implement hybrid retrieval systems combining keyword search, dense vector similarity, and reranking.
Build and maintain Elasticsearch indexing pipelines, query services, and relevance tuning tooling.
Integrate vector databases (Pinecone, Weaviate, FAISS or similar) into retrieval workflows—even if this is new territory, you'll learn fast.
Instrument search pipelines with meaningful metrics: CTR, zero-result rate, latency—feeding the team's A/B experimentation loop.
Build clean, responsive, and production-ready interfaces from wireframes or Figma designs.

Own the Engineering Bar

Champion CI/CD, observability, testing, and infrastructure-as-code as non-negotiables, not afterthoughts.
Lead design sessions with Engineers and Architects; translate product requirements into clean, maintainable technical solutions.
Participate in code reviews and knowledge-sharing—actively raising the team's collective skill level.

What You Bring

Must-Haves

Strong Python and React foundation: 6+ years of professional backend or full-stack engineering experience with a deep Python/React (e.g., Next.js, Vite.js, Remix.js, Gatsby.js) focus—async patterns, type annotations, testing, and production-grade service/component design.
Cloud-native experience: Proven experience designing and deploying cloud-native applications (

GCP strongly preferred; AWS or Azure considered).

Hands-on experience building resilient high throughput microservices and RESTful/gRPC APIs.
Solid understanding of containerization (Docker), orchestration (Kubernetes), and serverless paradigms.
Strong grounding in SOLID design principles and software craftsmanship.
Good communicator who thrives in cross-functional, agile teams alongside ML engineers, architects, and product owners.
Comfort using AI tools to accelerate development throughput.
Strong experience of using and managing Monorepos
Strong understanding of relational (e.g., PostgreSQL, MySQL, Oracle) and non-relational databases (e.g., MongoDB, DynamoDB).

Strongly Preferred — Search & ML

You don't need all of these on day one—but the more you bring, the faster you'll contribute:

Search systems: Experience with search platforms:

Elasticsearch, OpenSearch, Solr, or Algolia—index management, query DSL, relevance tuning.

Vector search: Familiarity with vector search concepts and tooling:

embeddings, approximate nearest neighbor (ANN), FAISS, Pinecone, Weaviate, or similar.

Exposure to ML/AI patterns: RAG pipelines, LLM integration, prompt engineering, or fine-tuning workflows.
Experience with AI orchestration frameworks such as LangChain, LangGraph, or Google ADK.
Infrastructure-as-code experience (Terraform, Pulumi, OpenTofu) and mature CI/CD pipeline ownership.

Who You Are

Fearless Builder

A working proof-of-concept beats a thousand slide decks. Speed and quality are both non-negotiable.

Relentless Learner

You pick up new technologies fast and have a genuine eagerness to master whatever comes next.

Architecture-Minded

You design scalable, fault-tolerant services as second nature and aren't afraid to challenge the status quo.

Ownership-Driven

Code isn't done until it's tested, documented, and monitored. Your name on a release means something.

Search-Curious

You may not have built a search system yet—but you're excited by the challenge and ready to go deep.

Team Multiplier

You give and welcome candid feedback and actively make the people around you better.

Stratolaunch accelerates the development of next-generation aerospace and defense technologies through reusable hypersonic flight testing. Our autonomous, air-launched Talon-A vehicles provide access to operationally realistic flight environments at speeds exceeding Mach 5, delivering critical data that helps customers validate system performance and advance technologies toward deployment. Our team brings together expertise in engineering, manufacturing, and flight operations to solve complex challenges and advance capabilities essential to national security.

The AI Solutions Engineer
contributes to the development, integration, and operation of AI capabilities across Stratolaunch. The Enterprise Software Team integrates a mix of COTS and custom tools to provide the right data, functionality, and AI-enabled capabilities to the right user at the right time.

This position will focus on the infrastructure, integrations, observability, and developer tools required to operationalize AI for vehicle design, manufacture, flight test, and business teams. Responsibilities may include hosting and maintaining large language model (LLM) and Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) systems; developing logging and monitoring capabilities; operating AI workloads in AWS; optimizing vector search systems such as Qdrant; and building APIs, plugins, SDKs, and command-line tools for internal users.

The AI Platform and MLOps Engineer will also evaluate and integrate COTS solutions, third-party services, open-source tools, and internally developed applications. Potential applications include meeting summarization and scheduling, CAD integrations, OpenWebUI and Hugging Face tools, team-specific plugins, and reusable software development kits. The scope of this position may be tailored to the selected candidate’s interests and experience, with particular opportunity for candidates experienced in ML workload optimization and cloud-based model operations.

Essential Responsibilities

Design, deploy, and operate reliable infrastructure for ML, LLM, and RAG workloads, with a focus on running and optimizing models in AWS and supporting future AI compute requirements.
Host, maintain, monitor, and optimize RAG systems, including Qdrant and other retrieval infrastructure, while developing the logging, observability, and alerting needed to assess system health, performance, cost, and reliability.
Serve as a subject matter expert for MLOps and AI workload operations, including model deployment, inference services, resource utilization, and production support.
Integrate and support COTS products, third-party services, open-source tools, and custom AI capabilities, sharing responsibility for their monitoring, security, cost, performance, and reliability.
Develop APIs, plugins, and reusable integrations that make AI capabilities available to Stratolaunch teams, including tools for OpenWebUI, Hugging Face, Wilbur, and other applicable platforms.
Collaborate with internal stakeholders to develop team-specific AI integrations and workflows, and to deliver practical interfaces between AI services and existing applications, including frontend applications, Streamlit services, NGINX load balancers, and other web infrastructure.
Collaborate with software, data, infrastructure, security, and domain teams to evaluate AI technologies and deliver maintainable, user-focused solutions.

Qualifications

Experience designing, deploying, and operating reliable, observable software or ML systems in production.
Experience with ML workloads, cloud infrastructure, and model deployment, preferably in AWS.
Experience with one or more programming languages, such as Python, Rust, C, MATLAB, or equivalent.
Experience developing and integrating APIs, services, plugins, or other software interfaces.

Experience with logging, monitoring, troubleshooting, and production support.
Comfort with CLI tools and shell scripting, such as Bash or Windows batch scripting.
Knowledge of DevSecOps and CI/CD systems, such as Jenkins, GitLab, Bamboo, or equivalent tools.
Experience integrating COTS products, third-party services, APIs, or open-source software into production environments.
Ability to collaborate with stakeholders to evaluate technical options and deliver practical solutions.

Preferred

MLOps experience, including hosting, maintaining, monitoring, and optimizing LLM and RAG systems.
Experience running models and inference workloads in AWS, including services such as EC2, Lambda, ECS, EKS, S3, and CloudWatch.
Experience optimizing RAG systems, vector databases, and retrieval pipelines, including Qdrant.

Education & Experience

5-10 years professional experience in software engineering, cloud infrastructure, data engineering, MLOps, AI engineering, or a related discipline.
$142,000-$165,000

No travel required
