About Pockyt

Pockyt is building the AI-native infrastructure for global money movement. We give merchants a single platform to accept payments from anywhere, send money globally, and manage funds through Global Virtual Accounts and stablecoins — but our ambition runs deeper than the rails themselves. We're architecting the connective tissue that lets money move across borders the way information moves across the internet: instantly, intelligently, and autonomously.

We serve a wide spectrum of merchants, from sophisticated enterprise platforms running complex multi-currency operations to the next generation of AI-powered startups, including the one-person unicorns we believe are about to reshape the global economy. Today, that means one integration, one account view, and one place to track everything. Tomorrow, it means a financial layer that AI agents can natively transact on — where money flows are orchestrated, optimized, and reconciled without human bottlenecks.

Our mission is to make global commerce frictionless. We're not building another payments platform. We're building the operating system for how value moves in an agentic, borderless economy.

The Role

We're hiring a Founding Engineer to start our New York Applied AI team — the small, senior, AI-leveraged group whose mandate is to compress quarters into days across Pockyt. This is our second engineering hire and our first engineering leadership hire in NYC. You'll set the bar for who joins next and lay down the patterns a 20x engineering org will inherit.

Your charter is agentic systems and applied AI, deployed wherever the highest-leverage workflow lives. The work begins inside the company because that's where the friction is most visible and the wins are most measurable — manual payment processing, compliance reviews, RFI loops, merchant onboarding, settlement reconciliation, treasury operations, and merchant configuration are full of workflows waiting to be replaced with agents. But the work doesn't stay there. The patterns you prove on our own operations are the same patterns we expose to merchants as Pockyt becomes the financial layer AI agents transact on. What you build here becomes the substrate.

This is a founder-mode builder-leader role. You'll own critical systems end-to-end, lead technical discovery on ambiguous problems, set the standards the engineers behind you will inherit, and mentor the team as it grows. You'll report directly to our CEO and collaborate closely with our Head of Product and the other technical leaders driving execution — Head of Product Engineering, Head of Engineering Operations, and Chief Architect — on system design, rollout, and how this team plugs into the rest of engineering.

If you've been waiting for the role where you get to build the self-improving company — instrument it, automate it, and watch the feedback loops compound until they reach the merchant — this is it.

What You'll Do

Own the applied AI and agentic workflow surface end-to-end: discovery, design, prototyping, production rollout, measurement, and iteration
Embed with Finance, Compliance, Ops, GTM, Support — and increasingly with merchants — to identify the workflows with the highest leverage and replace them with agents and software: reconciliation, KYC/EDD review queues, RFI triage, payment initiation, merchant configuration, reporting pipelines
Build durable, observable agentic systems: LLM-orchestrated workflows with retries, evals, rollback, and instrumentation that survive contact with real money movement
Graduate the highest-leverage workflows into merchant-facing product capability — the agent that reconciles our books becomes the agent merchants run on theirs
Set the technical foundation the broader Applied AI org will build on — eval frameworks, agent guardrails, prompt and tool design conventions, shared SDKs (some of which become merchant-facing), observability standards
Mentor and pair with the engineers who join behind you; raise the bar on code review, testing, and shipping discipline; help interview, hire, and onboard each new team member
Partner with the Chief Architect on guardrails for AI-generated code and agent-executed actions touching ledgers, settlements, and customer funds
Define success metrics for every system you ship — hours saved, manual payments eliminated, time-to-resolution, error rates, merchant time-to-value — and own the outcome publicly
Translate ambiguous executive asks into shipped systems; close the loop by demoing what's live and what's next

What We're Looking For

6+ years building production software, with a clear track record of owning critical systems end-to-end and shipping outcomes — not just features
Deep AI fluency — you use Claude, Cursor, Codex, and LLM/agent frameworks (LangGraph, Inngest, Temporal, browser automation, eval tooling, etc.) as a daily force multiplier and have opinions about when each one helps
Strong full-stack instincts across Java, TypeScript (Vue), and Golang, with comfort moving across frontend, backend, data plumbing, and integrations; depth in one area is fine, rigidity in only one is not
Experience designing agentic or workflow systems that touch real-world state (payments, ledgers, customer data) with safety, idempotency, observability, and rollback as first-class concerns
A history of operating without a backlog — you spot the problem, scope it, ship it, measure it, and move on
Demonstrated ability to mentor, set technical direction, and elevate the engineers around you; you've been the person whose patterns the rest of the team copies
Excellent written and verbal communication — you'll present to executives weekly and write specs and post-mortems for non-engineers
Genuine curiosity about how the business actually runs, and the patience to sit with ops, finance, and compliance to understand the workflow before automating it

Bonus Points

Prior experience as an early or founding engineer at a fast-moving startup, or as the technical lead for a forward-deployed / applied AI / platform team
Experience in fintech, cross-border payments, digital wallets, merchant acquiring, treasury, or financial reconciliation
Background in RegTech, compliance automation, KYC/KYB workflows, or transaction monitoring
Hands-on experience building eval pipelines and regression tests for LLM systems in production
Track record of recruiting and hiring engineers into a small, senior, AI-native team

Why Pockyt

Build at the frontier of AI + payments at a company shipping for both enterprise platforms and the next generation of AI-native merchants
Real ownership and direct work with senior leadership from day one — and a leading hand in building the team that comes after you
A clear path into engineering leadership (Staff, Head of Product Engineering, Head of Engineering Operations) as the surface area expands
Competitive compensation, employer-paid health insurance, 401(k) match, and unlimited PTO
Quarterly bonus pay-outs of up to 20% your base salary
Eligibility for founding team equity grant, vesting over 4 years with a 1-year cliff (subject to Board approval)

How You'll Work

Rhythm:
Rapid ideation → scoped prototype (hours/days) → pilot → production hardening → measure and iterate; weekly executive demos
Collaboration:
Daily collaboration with product, design, ops, finance, and compliance stakeholders; close partnership with Chief Architect on guardrails and Head of Product Engineering on rollout
Quality bar:
Ship small, safe, observable changes with clear rollback; instrument every workflow with outcome metrics; build evals before you scale anything LLM-driven
Team building:
Set the hiring bar, run technical interviews, and onboard the engineers who join behind you

Success looks like:
measurable elimination of manual hours across Finance, Compliance, and Ops in your first quarter; a documented library of agents and workflow patterns the rest of the company builds on; the first systems you ship graduating into merchant-facing capability; a clear, repeatable hiring and onboarding playbook for the NYC team; and the rest of the company asking what you'll automate next.

added.title: Forward Deployed Engineer
added.description:
Overview

Intuit Enterprise Suite is how the world's fastest-growing mid-market and enterprise finance teams run their books, close their quarter, and put AI agents to work on real accounting operations — not demos. Forward Deployed Engineers (FDEs) are the team that makes that real: embedded with our customers, shipping production automation, and turning “AI pilot” into “AI in the general ledger.”

This isn't a traditional sales engineering role, and it isn't a traditional product engineering role either. FDEs report into Engineering, work shoulder-to-shoulder with Sales and Account Management on the deals and renewals that matter most, and own the last mile between what Core Engineering ships and what a specific customer actually runs. You'll sit at the intersection of engineering, applied AI, and enterprise finance, and you'll be judged on one thing: did the customer's business measurably change because you were in the room.

Responsibilities

What you'll do

Pre-sale: build the proof that wins the deal

Get hands-on with prospects before there's a contract: build a working proof-of-value directly in (or against a realistic replica of) the prospect's own data and systems — real integrations and real output, not a scripted demo.
Partner with Account Executives from first technical touch: run discovery with the prospect's finance and IT teams to understand their chart of accounts, systems, and process gaps well enough to build against them.
Lead the technical evaluation: architecture and security/compliance reviews, integration feasibility, and technical RFP responses with the prospect's IT and controllership teams.
Build the technical narrative and ROI case alongside Sales, and present it directly to economic buyers — CFOs and Controllers — as part of the deal cycle. Your proof-of-value is very often what gets the deal signed.
Flag technical or data-readiness risk early, so Sales scopes and prices the deal accurately and nothing you built pre-sale becomes a surprise post-signature.

Post-sale: architect and ship in customer specific production

Architect and deploy customer-specific configurations of AI Agents that automate complex accounting processes — strengthening internal controls, closing books faster, and removing manual work from real customer environments.
Perform deep technical troubleshooting: review and edit Python, write SQL for integrations, and diagnose configuration issues across customer systems.
Serve as the functional and technical escalation point for issues involving integrations, data flows, and automation logic — including reviewing and optimizing SQL-based validations and API-driven workflows.
Maintain SLAs for response and resolution; document issues comprehensively and escalate to Engineering with complete context.

Post-sale: own the customer relationship and drive expansion

Lead high-impact transformation engagements with enterprise finance teams — diagnosing operational bottlenecks and identifying where AI Agents create the most leverage.
Act as the primary technical point of contact across implementations, engaging directly with CFOs, Controllers, and accounting leaders.
Guide and train customer teams through workflow redesign, change management, and the value realization required to scale AI Agent adoption across their organization — and carry that same proof-of-value discipline into expansion and renewal conversations.
Travel to customer sites as needed (up to 30-40%) for pre-sale technical evaluation, hands-on deployment, training, and adoption workshops.

Ongoing: shape the product and the playbook

Be the Voice of the Customer: surface technical feedback, integration requirements, and product gaps to Product and Core Engineering — as input to their roadmap, not a substitute for it.
Partner with Product Management on learnings from onsite discovery sessions to design workflows centered on AI Agent deployment and business outcomes.
Build the playbook: create implementation guides, expansion frameworks, and reusable assets so every deployment makes the next one faster.
Educate customers and internal teams on the strategic value of AI-enabled workflow transformation and best practices for building durable AI Agents.

Where this role sits

FDEs report into Engineering, not Sales — but this is very much a field role, spanning both sides of the signature, and the two partnerships below are the job as much as the code is.

Your partnership with Sales & Account Management

You're the technical face of Enterprise Suite in the field, on both sides of the deal: Account Executives pull you in pre-sale to build the proof-of-value that wins the technical evaluation, and Customer Success pulls you in post-sale for QBRs, renewals, and expansion.
Deals and renewals in this business run on proof, not promises — you're the one who produces it, first as a working pilot in the sales cycle, then as a live production system afterward. That makes you directly responsible for de-risking the pipeline, even though you don't carry a number yourself.
You'll work daily with Account Executives and Customer Success on the accounts you're assigned to; you won't be measured on bookings, but expect to be in the room for the technical parts of both the sale and the renewal.

Your partnership with Core Engineering

You build on top of what Core Engineering ships — you're not a parallel path to the platform roadmap, and this role doesn't re-architect the core product.
Architect and deploy customer-specific configurations of AI Agents that automate complex accounting processes — strengthening internal controls, closing books faster, and removing manual work from real customer environments. Candidates should have hands-on experience with agentic AI workflows (using, configuring, or building agents/tools)
Your job is the last-mile layer: wiring existing AI Agent capabilities into one customer's specific data, workflows, and edge cases, fast enough to prove value inside a live deal.
In return, you feed Core Engineering structured signal — the patterns that show up across multiple customers — so they can decide what to productize. FDE work should make the core roadmap sharper, never duplicate it or bypass it.

Qualifications

What you'll bring

Required

5 to10+ years in Forward Deployed Engineering, Solutions Engineering, Sales Engineering, technical consulting, or a comparable hands-on, customer-embedded engineering role (scope and level matched to experience — see Levels & Compensation below).
Deep experience with Agentic AI: LangChain, LangGraph, MCP servers, multi-agent, RAG, vector stores, hybrid retrieval
Experience with LLMs & tooling: OpenAI, Gemini, Anthropic; GitHub Copilot, Gemini Code Assist; prompt engineering
Deep experience with REST APIs, GraphQL, webhooks, SQL, and enterprise integrations.
Strong technical fluency and the ability to collaborate deeply with Product Managers and Engineers as a peer, not a hand-off.
A track record of managing multiple technical deployments simultaneously under delivery pressure.
Comfort leading technical troubleshooting calls with customers and internal IT teams.
Comfortable operating on both sides of the signature — building a credible proof-of-value under sales-cycle time pressure, and running that same system reliably in production afterward.
You default to automation — you use AI and modern tooling to move faster, document better, and scale your own impact.
Demonstrated ability to translate ambiguity into executable requirements, and to communicate insights clearly to both engineers and executives.
Strong commercial awareness, stakeholder management, and the ability to operate effectively under delivery and revenue pressure.

Preferred

Background in high-growth SaaS, applied AI, or fintech/ERP/accounting-adjacent domains.
Domain experience in one of our priority verticals — construction (job costing, WIP, retainage), nonprofit (fund accounting, grant and donor compliance), manufacturing (inventory, cost accounting, production workflows), wealth management (client billing, compliance/regulatory reporting, investment accounting), health care (revenue cycle, compliance-heavy financial operations), franchise (zee governance, zor performance), or field services (job/work-order costing, scheduling-linked billing). You don't need more than one, but depth in any single vertical materially shortens ramp-up on real customer engagements.
Non-traditional paths are a plus: veterans, former management consultants, competitive programmers, and PhDs have historically made excellent FDEs.
Prior experience embedded at a customer site for a multi-month deployment (implementation consulting, forward-deployed, or field engineering background).

Job Description Summary

The Senior AI Solutions Engineer advances the practical, responsible adoption of artificial intelligence across Miami University by connecting institutional needs with shared AI services, technical teams, and implementation partners.

This role combines hands-on technical fluency with consultation, solution delivery, and relationship building. You will help design and operate shared AI capabilities, guide academic and administrative units from ideas through pilots and sustainable solutions, and establish repeatable technical and operational patterns that allow AI services to scale securely and effectively. Working across organizational boundaries, you will coordinate with security, architecture, infrastructure, service owners, academic partners, and institutional AI groups while exercising significant independent judgment in a rapidly changing environment.

The position contributes implementation expertise to institutional AI governance but is primarily accountable for delivering usable services, enabling partners, and turning emerging AI capabilities into practical outcomes.

Job Description

Duties

Lead the design, implementation, rollout, and continuous improvement of shared University AI services within the perspective and purview of the Information Technology Services Division, including managed access to enterprise generative AI platforms, service gateways, account and domain administration, and related operating practices.
Serve as a consultative point of entry for academic and administrative units exploring AI-enabled solutions; clarify needs, assess feasibility, value, risk, and supportability, and recommend practical paths forward.
Prototype, configure, and integrate AI-enabled solutions when appropriate, and coordinate with technical teams and vendors to move promising pilots toward stable, supportable services.
Partner with units responsible for information security, legal, procurement, accessibility, architecture, data governance, and service owners to translate institutional requirements into practical technical and operational controls.
Develop reusable processes, service definitions, intake processes, financial/chrage-back models, documentation, and guardrails for common AI use cases.
Build and maintain awareness of significant AI initiatives across University divisions; connect teams, and encourage consistent approaches.
Collaborate with the University AI Center of Excellence, AI fellows, IT leaders, and other campus partners to support coordinated adoption and help build communities of practice for people applying AI in their work.
Create the framework to evaluate emerging AI technologies, and apply that framework to models, platforms, and vendors; communicate capabilities, limitations, tradeoffs, and recommendations to technical and non-technical audiences.
Establish and monitor measures for service adoption, reliability, support needs, and outcomes, and use those measures to improve AI services and consulting practices.
Contribute implementation experience and technical perspective to institutional AI governance efforts and help translate approved guidance into workable service and technology practices.
Develop and maintain business cases, including detailed financial evaluations, of proposed solutions.

Minimum Qualifications

Bachelor's degree by date of hire and 6+ years of related professional technical experience.

Or

Relevant Master's degree by date of hire AND 4+ years of related professional technical experience.

Experience may come from roles such as senior business analyst, technical lead, solutions architect, or similar positions.

Knowledge, Skills, And Abilities (KSAs)

Ability to rapidly learn, evaluate, and apply emerging artificial intelligence technologies in a practical enterprise environment.
Ability to build credibility, partnerships, and alignment across organizational boundaries without relying on formal authority.
Ability to translate ambiguous business, academic, or operational needs into clear technical options and supportable solutions.
Ability to move cross-functional initiatives from idea through pilot and enterprise implementation with a high degree of independence and sound judgment.
Working knowledge of generative AI concepts, large language models, APIs and integrations, identity and access management, data handling, and common security and privacy considerations.
Ability to communicate AI capabilities, limitations, risks, and tradeoffs clearly to both technical and non-technical audiences.
Ability to balance innovation and speed with security, privacy, accessibility, reliability, maintainability, and institutional requirements.
Ability to prioritize and manage multiple concurrent initiatives in a fast-changing environment.
Ability to facilitate consultations, demonstrations, workshops, and collaborative working sessions.
Ability to create clear documentation, reusable patterns, and service practices that improve consistency and organizational learning.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience implementing, administering, or supporting enterprise generative AI services such as ChatGPT, Claude, Microsoft Copilot, Google Gemini, Azure OpenAI, AWS Bedrock, or similar platforms.
Experience with large language model APIs and common AI solution patterns such as retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), agents, embeddings, vector search, or workflow automation.
Experience prototyping or integrating technology solutions using Python, JavaScript, APIs, low-code platforms, or similar tools.
Experience with enterprise identity and access management, SaaS/cloud administration, and information security practices.
Experience in technical consulting, evaluating technology vendors, technology service ownership, product management, or solution delivery across multiple stakeholder groups.
Experience building business cases, piloting emerging services, and moving successful pilots into sustainable operational support.
Experience facilitating communities of practice, training, workshops, or other peer-learning approaches.
Experience working in higher education or another complex, decentralized organization.

added.title: Sr. SW Engineer - AI Security
added.description:
About Us

Visa is a world leader in payments technology, facilitating transactions between consumers, merchants, financial institutions and government entities across more than 200 countries and territories, dedicated to uplifting everyone, everywhere by being the best way to pay and be paid.

At Visa, you'll have the opportunity to create impact at scale — tackling meaningful challenges, growing your skills and seeing your contributions impact lives around the world.

Join Visa and do work that matters – to you, to your community, and to the world. Progress starts with you.

Job Description

Visa's Cyber Analytics and AI Innovation organization builds the security capabilities that let the enterprise adopt Generative AI responsibly and safely. This is an innovation-oriented team: our charter evolves as GenAI threats evolve, and our core service is a growing suite of guardrail services that protects AI applications, LLMs, agents, tools, and data interactions from AI-specific threats.

As a Senior Software Engineer, GenAI Security, you'll be a hands-on individual contributor who owns problems end-to-end — from technical design and prototyping through production deployment, monitoring, and support. Because this is an innovation org, you won't be boxed into one feature lane: your work may span detection engines, agent and tool security, evaluation frameworks, or platform integration as priorities shift, and you'll often be handed a problem with real latitude in how you solve it rather than a fixed spec.

Essential Functions

Build and operate GenAI security systems: design, build, deploy, and maintain production services and APIs that detect and mitigate risks such as prompt injection, jailbreak attempts, sensitive-data exposure, and unauthorized or unexpected tool/agent behavior — spanning LLMs, agents, tools, APIs, MCP servers, plugins, and enterprise data sources. Apply deterministic, policy-driven controls where predictable enforcement matters, and model-based approaches where judgment is needed.
Measure and improve: build automated evaluation, testing, and feedback loops, plus production observability (logging, metrics, tracing, alerting, dashboards), so detection quality, latency, and false-positive/negative rates stay visible and auditable — then use that telemetry to close gaps.
Integrate and scale: containerize and deploy services with Docker and Kubernetes, and integrate GenAI security capabilities into enterprise applications, model gateways, developer workflows, and cloud or on-premises platforms.
Practice secure engineering: apply threat modeling, secure coding, dependency and secrets management, code review, and vulnerability remediation; participate in architecture and design reviews and document decisions, interfaces, and operational requirements clearly.
Explore and influence: evaluate emerging GenAI security technologies and frameworks through structured proofs of concept, provide technical guidance to other engineers, and help shape the team's engineering standards and practices.
Collaborate and operate: work with engineers, researchers, architects, product managers, and infrastructure teams to translate emerging AI-security risks into product capabilities, and support production releases, incident analysis, and defect resolution.

Position Location

This position may be based in Ashburn, Virginia, under Visa's hybrid working model. The expectation for days in the office will be confirmed by the hiring manager.

No relocation budget is available for this position.

Visa requires at least 3 days in office, expectations of these days will be confirmed by your Hiring Manager.

Qualifications

Basic Qualifications

2+ years of relevant work experience and a Bachelors degree, OR 5+ years of relevant work experience
Professional software-development experience building backend services, APIs, platforms, or distributed applications.
Experience developing production software using Python, Java, Go, or another modern programming language.
Experience with cybersecurity, secure software development, application security, cloud security, AI security, or a closely related discipline.

Preferred Qualifications

Advanced degree (M.S. or Ph.D.) in computer science, applied math, or a related field.
Strong proficiency in Python and at least one additional language such as Java, Go, or Rust, with solid grounding in distributed-systems fundamentals — software architecture, design patterns, data structures, concurrency, API design, and performance optimization — applied to highly available RESTful, asynchronous, or event-driven services.
Hands-on experience with Generative AI application architectures, including LLM APIs, embeddings, agentic workflows, tool calling, model gateways, and orchestration frameworks such as LangChain, LangGraph, Semantic Kernel, AutoGen, or LlamaIndex, along with familiarity with MCP, AI-agent tools, plug-ins, or similar emerging integration patterns.
Understanding of GenAI-specific security risks (prompt injection, jailbreaking, sensitive-data exposure, insecure output handling, unauthorized tool use, data exfiltration) and hands-on experience implementing controls such as input validation, output filtering, policy enforcement, access control, audit logging, rate limiting, and secrets management.
Knowledge of secure software-development lifecycle practices — threat modeling, vulnerability management, and application-security principles — applied in day-to-day engineering.
Experience developing evaluation frameworks or test suites for LLM applications, including adversarial or red-team testing, regression testing, and false-positive/false-negative analysis.
Experience with cloud-native deployment and operations — Docker, Kubernetes, CI/CD, infrastructure automation, and observability platforms (such as Splunk, Elasticsearch, or Grafana) for metrics, logging, tracing, alerting, and production troubleshooting.
Familiarity with GPU-backed inference, CUDA, NVIDIA technologies, or model-serving frameworks is beneficial but not required.
Ability to evaluate new technologies objectively against security, quality, latency, scalability, maintainability, and operational-readiness criteria, and to work independently on ambiguous, complex assignments.
Clear written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to explain technical and security tradeoffs to different audiences, and experience collaborating effectively in Agile, cross-functional environments spanning engineering, cybersecurity, infrastructure, research, and product.

added.title: Senior Staff Data Scientist, Product Data Science (Mailchimp)
added.description:
Overview

The Mailchimp Product Data Science team turns product and customer data into insights and models that shape Mailchimp's product strategy. We work as thought partners with Product, Design, Engineering, Marketing, Finance, and Pricing to drive data-driven decisions through experimentation, causal measurement, and deep customer analytics.

We're looking for a Senior Staff Data Scientist to be an analytical leader for Mailchimp's product growth. In this high-impact individual contributor role, you'll set the measurement vision across the full customer journey: sign-up and onboarding, activation, conversion to paid, engagement, and long-term retention. The role raises the scientific bar for how we experiment and size opportunities, and it shapes product and business strategy at the senior leadership level. It's also hands-on, focused on the highest-leverage problems and on helping the team adopt AI-native workflows that let us move faster.

This role is based in New York, NY / Mountain View, CA / Atlanta, GA under Intuit's hybrid model, 3 days per week in office.

Responsibilities

Influence product strategy: Be a strategic thought partner to senior Product and business leaders. Shape Mailchimp's growth roadmap with deep dives into customer segmentation, onboarding and activation funnels, feature adoption, pricing and packaging, and retention.
Set the analytics vision: Own the measurement framework, north-star and guardrail metrics, and leading indicators for the self-serve customer journey, from free and trial sign-ups to paid conversion, bookings, and recurring revenue.

added.title: Research Scientist II
added.description:
Akima Systems Engineering, an Akima company, is hiring a Research Scientist II in Madison, W
I to collaborate with government scientists and team members to develop and lead studies as outlined below.

The National Wildlife Health Center (NWHC) is a science center of the U.S. Geological Survey (USGS) with specialized laboratories dedicated to wildlife disease detection, control, and prevention. Their mission is to advance wildlife health science for the benefit of animals, humans, and the environment. Their work involves the coordination of research programs to study the use of vaccines to mitigate disease in wild bats, including white-nose syndrome and rabies.

WNS is an often-fatal disease of hibernating bats caused by Pseudogymnoascus destructans , a fungus introduced to North America from Eurasia. The disease was first documented in 2006 near Albany, New York and has since spread across most of the U.S. and Canada, killing millions of bats. Several bat species in the eastern U.S. are now threatened with extinction due to the disease, while many more bat species in the western part of the country are at risk as the fungus continues to spread. The position involves coordination of numerous state and federal partners and NGO’s in deploying vaccination at selected sites, prioritized by the US Fish and Wildlife Service and monitoring the population impacts of vaccination in comparison to sites that are not treated. Rabies is a fatal zoonotic disease that is transmitted by bats to humans and other animals. In South America, vampire bats are the primary vector of rabies for livestock in particular. Though not currently present in North America, their populations are expanding and vampire bats are expected to move north into Texas and or Florida with changing climate patterns. The work is to lead research to assess vaccination as a method to prevent rabies transmission by bats and to develop hands-off methods for vaccine deployment to bats for both WNS and rabies.

Responsibilities

The Research Scientist II will perform the tasks described below and within written established guidelines.
The work required is to perform a lead role in designing and conducting scientific experiments, generating scientific data, and providing appropriate analysis of data in support of experimental conclusions.
Experimental designs, hypotheses, results, and conclusions shall be documented, and records shall be submitted documenting progress towards task accomplishment.
Incumbents will collaborate with USGS staff and scientists to collect data, perform analyses, and write and publish USGS report products, in accordance with fundamental science practices and quality assurance standards.
Perform laboratory studies of fungal pathogens such as those that cause bat white-nose syndrome and snake fungal disease.
Relies on high level of experience, judgement, and innovation to perform both laboratory and field studies.
Perform and supervise others in the production of vaccine lots, testing and maintaining quality control standards throughout.
Act as a liaison to the USDA Center for Veterinary Biologics, the US Fish and Wildlife Service, and numerous other state and federal agencies for the distribution and application of vaccine to mitigate WNS in bats.
Prepare proposals to secure funding, manuscripts for publication, and give presentations at scientific meetings and to government and non-government partners involved in the research
Lead research studies on the impact of WNS vaccination and the feasibility of rabies vaccination of vampire bats.
Test various methods of vaccine deployment using hands-off approaches.
Create, edit, and follow standard operating procedures (SOPs), maintain a detailed laboratory notebook, and adhere to guidelines of a Quality Management System (QMS).
Operate laboratory equipment (balances, centrifuges, microscopes, incubators, shakers, pipettes, thermal cyclers, spectrophotometers).
Train and supervise others in trapping and handling of animals, collection of samples, and laboratory analyses of samples.
Assemble, evaluate, and analyze data for presentation in a scientifically appropriate manner.
Assemble, evaluate, and analyze data for inclusion in reports and publications describing results.
Maintain laboratory supplies and equipment and ensure all laboratory safety standards are met.

Qualifications

Must be a US citizen ablet to pass a thorough background check including criminal and financial at both the state and federal level (note this process can take at least 3 weeks to complete).
PhD in science related discipline.
3-4 years of experience.
Strong analytical, problem-solving and computer skills.
Experience leading various roles in laboratory or field research projects.
Experience planning and executing experiments and research; and summarizing findings in reports.

added.description:

Job Description

Brief Summary of Work for this Position

The Department of Mathematics and Statistics (http://www.uncw.edu/math) at the University of North Carolina Wilmington invites applications for a nine-month, tenure-track position at the rank of Assistant Professor in Data Science, starting Fall 2027. We seek a dynamic scholar whose teaching and research will support our growing data science programs while enriching the broader mathematical community.

The successful candidate will be expected to develop and maintain an active research program in data science or a closely related area, teach undergraduate and graduate courses supporting the department’s data science, mathematics, and statistics programs, and contribute to the continued development of the data science curriculum. Areas of particular interest include mathematical foundations of data science, optimization, machine learning, large language models, and artificial intelligence. The successful candidate will also contribute to student research and mentoring and participate in interdisciplinary collaborations across the university.

The department offers undergraduate programs in mathematics and statistics, and graduate programs in mathematics, statistics and data science. We are committed to supporting new faculty through mentorship, professional development, and a collaborative academic environment. We especially welcome candidates whose research, teaching, and service will contribute to the diversity, equity, and excellence of our academic community.

Minimum Education And Experience Requirements

A PhD in Mathematics, Applied Mathematics or a closely related field is required in order to be eligible for employment in this position.

Please note: ABD candidates will be considered; however, the PhD must be conferred by August 1, 2027, to be eligible for employment.

Preferred Education, Knowledge, Skills & Experience

Postdoctoral experience

Demonstrated interest in undergraduate and graduate research

Potential to collaborate with existing faculty on research

Teaching experience

Potential to secure external funding

Required Certifications or Licensure

No Required Certifications or Licensure

Primary Function of Organizational Unit

The department offers undergraduate programs in mathematics, statistics and data science, a certificate in actuarial science and graduate programs in mathematics and data science, as well as a post-baccalaureate certificate in statistics. The department and university are committed to assisting new faculty to succeed through continual faculty development and mentorship. The department is especially interested in qualified candidates who can contribute, through their teaching and service, to the diversity and excellence of the academic community.

College/School Information

The College of Science and Engineering offers a variety of programs leading to Bachelor of Science and Master of Science degrees, as well as Doctor of Philosophy degrees in applied coastal and ocean sciences; pharmaceutical chemistry; integrative, comparative, and marine biology; and psychology degrees. The college also offers combined bachelor’s/master’s degree programs in information technology/computer science and information systems, computer science/computer science and information systems, and B.S. in mathematics/M.S. in mathematics. To implement its academic programs, the college provides instruction and research opportunities in the natural and behavioral sciences, information technology, data science, computer science, mathematics, pre-engineering, and engineering. The eight academic departments in the college provide courses of study in each of these areas, in addition to interdepartmental programs in information technology, cybersecurity, and digital arts. A 2+2 in engineering; and 3+2 programs in computer science and electrical or computer engineering; and physics and electrical engineering, are also offered in the college. Post-baccalaureate certificate programs in environmental studies, applied statistics, and geographic information science are also available.

CSE students work with distinguished faculty and scientists, use cutting edge technology, and conduct impactful research. Faculty-directed research projects empower CSE students to apply what they learn inside the classroom and laboratory to real-world situations and prepares them for a variety of careers or advanced study.

University Information

The University of North Carolina Wilmington, the state’s coastal university, is dedicated to the integration of teaching, mentoring, research and service. Widely acknowledged for its world-class faculty and staff and continuously recognized at a national level for scholarly excellence and affordability, UNCW offers a powerful academic experience that stimulates creative inquiry and critical thinking.

A public institution with nearly 18,000 students, UNCW offers a full range of baccalaureate- and graduate-level programs, as well as doctoral degrees in educational leadership, marine biology, nursing practice and psychology; and many distance learning options, including clinical research, an accelerated RN-to-BSN program, an Executive M.B.A. program structured for working professionals, and the nation’s only bachelor’s degree program focused on coastal engineering.

The university’s efforts to advance research and scholarly activities have earned UNCW the elevated designation of “Doctoral Universities: High Research Activity” institution (R2 University) by the Carnegie Classification of Institutions of Higher Education.

UNCW has been part of the University of North Carolina System since 1969.

added.title: Sr. Staff Solutions Architect – Manufacturing (R6252)
added.description:
Shield AI is a venture-backed defense-tech company with the mission of protecting service members and civilians with intelligent systems. Its products include Hivemind autonomy software, V-BAT and X-BAT aircraft, and Aechelon simulation and synthetic reality technologies. With offices and facilities across the U.S., Europe, the Middle East, and Asia-Pacific, Shield AI’s technology actively supports operations worldwide. For more information, visit www.shield.ai . Follow Shield AI on LinkedIn , X , Instagram , and YouTube .

Shield AI is seeking a senior Solutions Architect – Manufacturing to serve as the functional and technical authority for Oracle Fusion Cloud ERP across Manufacturing, MRP/Supply Chain Planning, and the shop-floor-to-ERP technology stack. This role owns the design, configuration, and continuous improvement of Oracle Fusion Manufacturing and MRP capabilities, with deep, hands-on strength in MES, QMS, and PLM — ensuring plan, build, and quality processes operate as one coherent, well-architected system.

This is a hands-on, business-facing role. The Solutions Architect is expected to be the trusted advisor and go-to resource for Manufacturing and Quality business partners on any process change involving Oracle Fusion Manufacturing/Planning or the MES, QMS, and PLM bolt-on applications — translating business need into a scalable, well-architected solution, and then configuring and implementing that solution directly for medium-complexity projects. For large, complex initiatives, this person leads solution design and partners with Shield AI’s implementation partner to deliver, while remaining the accountable architect and voice of the business throughout.

Beyond core ERP, this role holds full ownership of Shield AI’s manufacturing-adjacent bolt-on application landscape — including MES, QMS, and PLM (Teamcenter) — and is responsible for how those systems integrate with Oracle Fusion ERP to form a coherent plan-to-build-to-quality operating model. This role partners closely with the other Solutions Architects for Supply Chain and Finance on shared MRP/planning signals, supplier quality matters tied to Procure-to-Pay and end-to-end integration with Finance/Accounting.

What you'll do:

Solution Architecture & Business Partnership

Designs and delivers technical solutions, creates detailed solution designs, specific integration points, and selects appropriate tools and frameworks. Collaboration with developers and engineers to implement solutions, conducts technical reviews and resolves design challenges.
Documents architectures, provides technical guidance during development, and ensures solutions adhere to performance, security, and interoperability requirements. Prototypes new approaches and evaluates emerging technologies for project suitability.
Serve as the primary point of contact and trusted advisor for business partners across Manufacturing, Production Planning, Quality, and Engineering on process design and system capability questions.
Act as the lead advocate for Manufacturing and Quality stakeholders in all ERP, MES, QMS, and PLM-related discussions, ensuring their operational needs, constraints, and priorities are represented in solution design.
Become the go-to resource for any proposed Manufacturing or Quality process change, evaluating impact, feasibility, and fit within the Oracle Fusion ERP data model and integration landscape before implementation.
Translate business requirements into scalable solution designs that balance standard Oracle Fusion functionality against configuration, extension, or integration needs.
Maintain a working command of adjacent end-to-end flows (Order-to-Cash, Procure-to-Pay) to ensure Manufacturing, MRP, MES, and QMS designs do not create downstream conflicts or gaps.

Hands-On Configuration & Delivery

Directly configure Oracle Fusion Manufacturing, Supply Chain Planning/MRP, Work Definitions, Quality Inspections, and related modules for medium-sized projects, enhancements, and break/fix work.
Build, test, and deploy configuration changes, including setup of Fusion functional areas, security, workflows, approval rules, and data structures related to manufacturing and planning processes.
Author functional design documents, configuration workbooks, test scripts, and process/procedure documentation to support changes made in the environment.
For large or highly complex initiatives, define solution architecture and requirements, then partner closely with the implementation partner to execute — remaining accountable for solution quality, business fit, and knowledge transfer.
Participate in and help lead workshops, fit-gap sessions, and design reviews with Manufacturing and Quality stakeholders and implementation partner teams.

MRP, MES & QMS Ownership

Own MRP and Supply Chain Planning configuration — planning parameters, supply/demand netting, exception messages, and planner workbench — ensuring plans translate cleanly into executable work orders.
Own the functional roadmap, configuration governance, and business alignment for:

– MES (Manufacturing Execution System) — work order execution, shop-floor data collection, routing/operation tracking

– QMS (Quality Management System) — inspections, non-conformance, corrective/preventive action (CAPA), supplier quality

– PLM – Teamcenter — engineering BOM, item master, and change management integration with Oracle Fusion

Ensure MES, QMS, and PLM remain architecturally aligned with Oracle Fusion Manufacturing and MRP, avoiding duplicate data ownership, conflicting BOM/routing data, or process gaps across systems.
Define and maintain the target integration model between MES, QMS, PLM, and Oracle Fusion ERP, including engineering-to-manufacturing BOM transfer and quality event-to-ERP disposition flows.
Partner with the Solutions Architect – Supply Chain on supplier-quality data flowing from Procure-to-Pay into QMS-driven supplier corrective action processes.

Integrations

Design and help implement integrations between Oracle Fusion ERP and MES, QMS, and PLM (Teamcenter), including BOM/routing sync, work order status, and quality disposition data.
Define integration requirements, data mappings, and error-handling/reconciliation approaches in partnership with technical/integration teams.
Evaluate integration patterns (API, middleware, file-based) and recommend approaches appropriate to data volume, latency, and criticality, particularly for shop-floor/real-time data.
Support testing, cutover, and hypercare activities for integration-related changes.

Governance & Continuous Improvement

Maintain configuration standards, documentation, and change control discipline for the Manufacturing, MRP, MES, QMS, and PLM functional areas.
Identify opportunities for process simplification, automation, and improved data quality across planning, production, and quality cycles.
Stay current on Oracle Fusion quarterly releases relevant to Manufacturing and Planning, and assess/recommend adoption of new features.
Mentor junior functional/technical resources and contribute to a growing internal ERP center of excellence.

Required Qualifications:

12+ years of progressive experience in enterprise ERP systems, with significant depth in MRP/Supply Chain Planning, MES, and QMS functions.
Hands-on experience configuring Oracle Fusion Cloud ERP (Manufacturing and Planning pillars); comfortable working directly in the application, not solely at a requirements level.
Experience across multiple full-lifecycle ERP implementations (Oracle Fusion required; prior experience with Oracle EBS, SAP, or other major ERP platforms is a plus).
Direct, hands-on experience with at least one MES platform and one QMS platform, including their integration into an ERP environment.
Working knowledge of Order-to-Cash and Procure-to-Pay processes and how they interact with Manufacturing, MRP, and quality operations.
Demonstrated experience acting as a functional/solution architect — able to design solutions independently, not just execute configuration tasks handed down by others.
Experience partnering with or managing systems integrators/implementation partners on complex delivery efforts.
Strong business partnering and stakeholder management skills; comfortable being the primary escalation point for Manufacturing and Quality process questions.
Working understanding of integration concepts and experience partnering on ERP-to-MES/QMS/PLM system integrations.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including experience producing functional design documents, process documentation, and executive-level updates.

Preferred Qualifications:

Prior consulting background (Big 4, Oracle partner, or boutique Oracle Fusion implementation firm) strongly preferred.
Direct experience owning or integrating PLM (Teamcenter) with Oracle Fusion Manufacturing/Engineering data.
Experience in aerospace, defense, or other regulated/complex discrete manufacturing environments.
Familiarity with Oracle Integration Cloud (OIC) or similar middleware/integration platforms.
Oracle Fusion certifications in Manufacturing, Supply Chain Planning, or Quality.
Experience operating in environments with export control, ITAR/CUI, or other regulated data-handling requirements.

AI & Agentic Automation Capabilities:

Shield AI is investing in Agentic AI to accelerate and automate manufacturing and quality operations. This role is expected to actively identify, design, and help implement AI-driven automation across Manufacturing, MRP, MES, and QMS — not simply consume AI tools built by others.

Identify high-value candidates for Agentic AI automation within Manufacturing and Quality — e.g., planner workbench exception triage, shop-floor anomaly detection, quality non-conformance routing/CAPA drafting, and work order scheduling recommendations.
Design and configure AI agent workflows using Oracle’s embedded AI/ML and agentic capabilities (e.g., Oracle Fusion AI agents, OCI Generative AI, Redwood/AI-driven planning recommendations) as they become available across Fusion Manufacturing and Planning.
Partner with IT/data teams to define prompts, guardrails, data inputs, and approval/exception paths for AI agents acting on manufacturing and quality transactions, ensuring appropriate human-in-the-loop controls.
Evaluate and pilot third-party or custom Agentic AI tools (e.g., for predictive maintenance, quality defect pattern detection, MES data synthesis, or supply/demand sensing) and assess fit against the target architecture.
Use AI-assisted tools for day-to-day solution work — requirements analysis, test script generation, configuration documentation, and data mapping — to increase delivery speed and quality.
Bring or build fluency in prompt engineering and AI workflow design; prior hands-on experience with generative AI or agentic AI platforms (Oracle AI Agent Studio, OCI Generative AI, Microsoft Copilot Studio, UiPath/Automation Anywhere agentic features, or similar) is a strong plus.
Champion responsible AI adoption — data quality, auditability, and change management — when introducing agentic workflows into regulated, ITAR/CUI-sensitive environments.

added.title: Senior Perception AI Engineer - Autonomous Vehicles
added.description:
Requirements

Self-driving cars need to understand the road ahead in real time, even without a prior map. Our team builds the online mapping system that turns raw data from multiple sensors into an accurate, continuously updated 3D model of the driving environment. This model captures lanes, road boundaries, crosswalks, intersection layouts, and traffic control information to support decisions across the autonomous driving system. You’ll write the models, write the C++, and ship both into vehicles on the road, running on NVIDIA DRIVE Orin and Thor. The tasks you perform will be tested at scale, on real cars, with real safety requirements. NVIDIA’s autonomous driving stack spans the full range of automation, and online mapping is a core component across it, so your work will reach L2++, L3, and L4 systems. The role spans two subject areas, and we want someone who enjoys both:

Learned mapping involves training DNNs to predict map elements directly from visual sensors, laser scanning, and radar. This includes owning the GT story and collaborating with partners to provide the vital data.
Geometry and C++ engineering: building the post-processing that turns network outputs into stable, consistent, production-ready map elements.

What You’ll Be Doing

Design, train, and improve PyTorch models that predict online map elements (lanes, road boundaries, crosswalks, road markings, topology) from camera, LiDAR, and/or radar, using BEV and vectorized-map representations.
Solve the hardest scenes: model intersection topology (connectivity between incoming and outgoing lanes, turn paths, merges and splits) and traffic light understanding (detection, state, and association of each light to the lanes it controls).
Write production C++ for geometry-based post-processing: curve and surface fitting, association, multi-frame fusion and tracking, topology reasoning, and consistency checks on DNN outputs.
Apply multi-view geometry, calibration, coordinate transforms, and sensor fusion to produce 3D maps that stay accurate and stable over time.
Optimize and deploy models alongside algorithms on NVIDIA DRIVE Orin and Thor under real-time and safety constraints, and get them running in vehicles.
Lead the narrative around GT and the data loop by planning datasets and defining GT and labeling requirements. Work with labeling, data, and tooling partners to produce high-quality GT. Mine data, choose metrics, and analyze failure cases to drive improvements.
Define critical metrics and build evaluation tooling to measure quality gains against large-scale real-world data.
Partner with perception, localization, planning, and infrastructure teams to integrate online mapping into the full AV stack, across L2++, L3, and L4 programs.
Contribute to technical direction and architecture decisions across the learned and geometric components of the mapping system.

What We Need To See

MS or PhD or equivalent experience in Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, Robotics, or a related field, or equivalent experience
5+ years of industry or research experience in autonomous driving, robotics, or computer vision.
Strong foundation in 3D geometry: camera models, projective geometry, coordinate transforms, optimization, and curve/surface fitting.
Strong C++ skills, with a track record of designing and shipping production-quality algorithm code that is fast, reliable, and maintainable.
Hands-on experience training deep neural networks in PyTorch, including model design, training pipelines, debugging, and performance analysis.
Experience with data-driven development: building datasets, defining labels and GT, choosing metrics, and improving models by analyzing failures.
Excellent problem-solving and communication skills, and the ability to drive technical direction across teams.

Ways To Stand Out From The Crowd

Direct experience with DNN-based online or HD map generation, or BEV perception (e.g., vectorized map prediction, lane topology learning), or equivalent experience to BEV perception.
Experience with intersection understanding, such as lane connectivity and topology reasoning in sophisticated junctions, or traffic light detection and lane association.
Experience combining learned models with geometric post-processing in a production AV system and publications or open-source contributions in 3D vision, mapping, or autonomous driving.
Background in sensor fusion, multi-object tracking, or temporal fusion for map elements.
Experience deploying DNNs and algorithms on embedded GPUs (CUDA, TensorRT), ideally on DRIVE Orin or Thor, under real-time constraints.

added.title: Staff Software Engineer, Agentic Analytics
added.description:
Who are we?

Cohere is the leading security-first enterprise AI company. We build cutting-edge foundation AI models and end-to-end products that are designed to solve real-world business problems.

We’re training and deploying frontier models for enterprises who are building AI systems. We believe that our work is instrumental to the widespread adoption of AI and we are looking for folks that want to be part of that.

We obsess over what we build. Each one of us is responsible for contributing to increasing the capabilities of our models and the value they drive for our customers. Cohere is a team of researchers, engineers, designers, and more, who are all passionate about their craft.

We are a global technology company headquartered in Toronto with key offices in London, New York City, San Francisco, Montreal, Paris, Berlin and Seoul. Join us!

Why this role?

We're building the foundational infrastructure that will define how the world thinks about and deploys AI, and we want the sharpest, most driven, and most curious people to help us do it. As the founding lead of Agentic Analytics, a new team in our Analytics and Data Insights organization, you'll own how Cohere gets answers from its own data: an agentic analytics system that answers business questions over governed data, shows the source, query, and freshness behind every answer, and asks for clarification or declines when the evidence is insufficient.

Agentic analytics is far from a solved problem, and correctness is the hard part. A query that runs can still answer the wrong question. Agents go wrong when a business term maps to more than one table, when data goes stale, and when the right context never reaches the model. The worst failures are silent and plausible: a join that double-counts, a wrong denominator, missing data read as zero. Getting this right takes governed definitions, context an agent can use, and an evaluation bar that decides what ships.

You'll build on work already in motion: an internal analytics agent in pilot on our BigQuery warehouse, which is fed by tested ingestion pipelines and modeled in dbt. In your first year, you'll take it to production for teams across Cohere, one domain at a time, and make it replicable: each new domain stands up with configuration, a fresh evaluation set, and very little new code.

This is a hands-on staff engineering role reporting to our Senior Director of Data Analytics. You'll write production code and evaluation sets yourself while managing a small founding team that grows as the system proves itself. You may have held the title software engineer, AI engineer, or data scientist; what matters is that you've built a system like this and run it in production.

Responsibilities

As the lead of Agentic Analytics, you will:

Own the system end to end. Set the architecture for how a business question becomes a governed query and a verifiable answer: interpreting the question, retrieving the right context, applying approved definitions and joins, enforcing the asking user's permissions, and attaching the evidence (source, query, freshness) to every answer.
Build and run it in production. Design the core services and write much of the first version yourself: agent-facing data tools (MCP or equivalent), context retrieval, agent skills for analytics, and the APIs that serve answers. Hold them to production standards for reliability, latency, cost, security, and observability. Put it where people already work: Slack, North, IDEs, and other agents.
Hold every release to the evaluation bar. Build and run the evaluation harness, and define what correct means in each domain: ground-truth question sets, including held-out cases and questions the agent should clarify or decline; result-level scoring, correct-or-decline rates, coverage, and error severity; and regression tests on every change to context, skills, or models. Nothing ships below the bar, and the call on when a domain is ready for production is yours.
Engineer the context layer. Turn metric definitions, approved joins, documentation generated from the code that builds each table, a business glossary, and worked examples into context the agent can use. Every correction becomes a reviewed definition and a regression test.
Roll it out across Cohere. Bring domains such as marketing, revenue, finance, and product onto the system one at a time, each with named owners, certified definitions, and its own evaluation set. Measure adoption, accuracy, turnaround, and correction effort against how those teams work today.
Make it replicable. Package the tools, skills, context templates, and evaluations, and document them well enough that other teams at Cohere can run the system without you.
Hire and lead the team. Bring on the team's first engineers, set the technical bar, review the work, and develop the people doing it.
Partner across Cohere. Work with our data platform team on the warehouse and semantic models, our model evaluation team on evaluation methodology, our security team on access, and each domain's owners on definitions and rollout.

Qualifications

You may be a good fit, if you have:

10+ years building and operating production analytics or software systems, including technical leadership of a team or of systems that span teams
Experience shipping LLM agents to production: tool use, MCP or similar, retrieval and context engineering, guardrails, and observability, with firm opinions on where they fail
Hands-on experience building natural-language or agentic analytics (text-to-SQL, analytics agents, question answering over a semantic layer) that real users relied on, and evidence that it was right
Depth in evaluating LLM systems: golden sets, result-level comparison, abstention metrics, error taxonomies, and regression testing in CI, plus the judgment to tell a good demo from a system you'd put in front of a CFO
Strong Python and SQL, and experience designing and running production services and APIs on a major cloud (Google Cloud is a plus)
Fluency with data: cloud warehouses (BigQuery, Snowflake, or similar), dbt, and semantic layers (MetricFlow, LookML, Cube, or similar). You think in grain, metric definitions, and approved joins, and you can tell when a number is wrong before it reaches a decision
Experience building identity-aware access for agents, where the agent acts with the asking user's permissions and every query leaves an audit trail
Experience hiring and developing engineers, with a leadership style grounded in empathy as much as in data
Genuine excitement about AI: you follow the research, have opinions, and enjoy being in the weeds
Comfort operating in ambiguity, leading through partners you don't manage, and writing design docs and eval reports that settle decisions across teams

If some of the above doesn't line up perfectly with your experience, we still encourage you to apply!

How And Where We Work

Cohere is remote-friendly, but we also have offices in Toronto, London, New York City, San Francisco, Montreal, Paris, Berlin and Seoul with more opening soon.

As an Applied Scientist specializing in Small Language Models and AI Training, you will lead research and development efforts focused on building efficient, high-performance language models tailored for practical applications. added.description:
ABOUT EARNIN
As one of the first pioneers of earned wage access, our passion at EarnIn is building products that deliver real-time financial flexibility for people living paycheck to paycheck. Our community members access their earnings as they earn them, with options to spend, save, and grow their money without mandatory fees, interest rates, or credit checks. We’re fortunate to have an incredibly experienced leadership team, combined with world-class funding partners like A16Z, Matrix Partners, DST, Ribbit Capital, and a very healthy core business with a tremendous runway. We’re growing fast and excited to bring on world-class talent to help shape the next chapter of our growth journey.
EarnIn is becoming an AI-native company, embedding AI agents into how we build, analyze, and operate across every function. Teams use AI Agents to move from ideas to execution faster. By letting agents handle repetitive tasks, our people can focus on judgment, creativity, and hard problems. We pair this experimentation with the strict review and security guardrails our regulated financial environment requires, always keeping a focus on privacy and the people who rely on our products.
As a company, we are becoming AI-native, and we encourage you to use AI tools throughout much of your interview process. If you use AI during the live interview, just say so; a quick, natural mention of how it helped and why you are using it is all we need. What we're evaluating is your judgment, reasoning, and ability to own and defend your work, not whether AI was involved. Some rounds, particularly those focused on your career history and past experiences, will not allow the use of AI, and we'll let you know of those in advance. When in doubt, ask your recruiter or interviewer directly.
POSITION SUMMARY

EarnIn is making AI-native engineering a core capability — not an initiative, but how we design, build, and ship. We're not hiring a software engineer who dabbles in AI. We're hiring an AI builder who also writes great software — someone who looks at every step of how we design, build, test, and ship, and asks: why isn't an agent doing this? This is not a side project. The agents and harnesses you build here will run in production, making real decisions for real people — people who depend on EarnIn to access their pay when it matters most. If that bar excites you rather than intimidates you, keep reading.
You'll work at the intersection of platform engineering, developer experience, and applied AI — partnering with architects, domain leads,, and product engineers to build the tools, patterns, and guardrails that make AI adoption fast, safe, and durable. The Mountain View base salary range for this full-time position is $228,000 - $279,000, plus equity and benefits. Our salary ranges are determined by role, level, and location. This is a hybrid position in Mountain View that requires in-office work 2 days a week. 
WHAT YOU'LL DO

Agents that take real actions. You'll design how agents think — prompts, reasoning chains, tool calls, and the full architecture beneath them. From MCP servers and agent scaffolding to context harnesses and a Skills Marketplace, you're building the layer every squad at EarnIn builds on. Not a proof of concept. Production infrastructure. 
A PDLC that doesn't look like 2022. The product development lifecycle is overdue for a rethink. You'll challenge each stage — from scoping and design through to review, testing, deployment, and monitoring — and replace manual friction with agentic workflows wherever it makes sense. Evaluation pipelines, automated PR hygiene, deployment gating, generation-to-merge metrics: you'll build the scaffolding that makes governed AI fast, not slow.
Evals that actually mean something. You'll own the evaluation infrastructure — building the pipelines, benchmarks, and quality gates that tell us whether our AI is working, degrading, or ready to ship. That means designing eval harnesses for AI-assisted workflows, setting generation-to-merge and review latency baselines, and making model quality visible and trustworthy across teams. If you've built evals that caught real problems before they hit production, you'll fit right in.
Pilots that graduate to production. EarnIn's engineering leads are running experiments. You'll be the person who takes what's working and turns it into something the next team can fork and ship in a week. Less "interesting prototype," more "thing we rely on." You’ll build reusable libraries, templates, and reference implementations that give squads a running start on AI integration, so no one has to solve the same problem twice
WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE

Teams across engineering can ship AI-assisted features faster, with fewer rework loops
The harnesses you build are actively used and well-documented
AI pilot quality and safety metrics are visible, trustworthy, and improving

WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

4+ years of full-time software engineering experience, with at least 2 years building tooling, platforms, or internal developer products

Experience in fintech or regulated/security-sensitive environments

Job Description

Research Engineer, Agentic Infrastructure

Legal Innovation through Frontier Technology Lab (liftlab), Stanford Law School

Stanford Law School’s Legal Innovation through Frontier Technology Lab (liftlab) is seeking a Research Engineer to design and implement the software systems that make the lab’s research possible. Working at the intersection of software engineering, computational research, and agentic AI, the engineer will build infrastructure for coordinating research agents, rapidly provisioning research environments, and running large-scale empirical experiments.

The Research Engineer reports to the lab Directors, Prof. Julian Nyarko and Dr. Megan Ma. The Directors collaboratively design the research agenda, study designs, and methodological requirements. The engineer develops the technical response to that design: assessing feasibility, contributing architectural and implementation ideas, translating research specifications into working systems, and iterating with the scientist as findings and requirements evolve.

The successful candidate will combine strong programming and systems architecture skills with an understanding of research methods and reproducibility. They will build modular, configurable infrastructure that allows researchers to vary models, datasets, agent strategies, and experimental conditions without rebuilding workflows from scratch. Their responsibilities will span the software development lifecycle, from technical design and prototyping through testing, deployment, maintenance, and performance optimization. Developing classifiers and baseline models will be part of a broader responsibility to turn collaboratively developed research ideas into reliable, adaptable computational capabilities.

Your Duties Will Include

Research Collaboration and Technical Design: Translate research designed with the Directors and other research scientists into technical specifications, implementation plans, and deliverable milestones. Assess feasibility, identify computational constraints, explain technical tradeoffs, and contribute design feedback that informs continued research development.
Agentic Infrastructure and Software Development: Design and implement modular systems for deploying and coordinating research agents, integrating models and tools, managing data, and executing experiments. Develop reusable interfaces and configuration-driven workflows that accommodate changes in research questions, methods, and experimental conditions.
Research Environments and Scalable Experimentation: Rapidly provision reproducible computing environments with appropriate software, dependencies, and data access. Build parallel or distributed experiment pipelines that support comparisons across datasets, models, prompts, and agent strategies, with appropriate logging, checkpointing, and recovery mechanisms.
Computational Methods and Validation: Implement classifiers, baseline models, analytical tools, and evaluation harnesses as research needs require. Read research papers and associated source code, test implementations against reference results, and collaborate with the research scientists and fellows to investigate discrepancies and validate computational behavior.
Software Quality and Reproducibility: Lead code review, automated testing, debugging, change control, and technical documentation. Establish practices for tracking code, data, model, configuration, and environment versions so that experiments can be reproduced and results traced to their computational inputs.
Operations and Performance: Maintain, troubleshoot, and upgrade research applications and infrastructure. Diagnose complex failures, evaluate libraries and platform changes, and optimize runtime, data access, scheduling, and resource use while preserving experimental conditions and reproducibility.
Technical Leadership and Collaboration: Lead engineering delivery, exercising independent technical judgment within agreed research requirements and priorities. Mentor research staff as needed; develop clear implementation guides; and collaborate with computing and data professionals on development standards, deployment practices, and infrastructure planning.

Preferred Education

A Master’s degree in computer science, software engineering, data science, computational methods, or a related field, strongly preferred. PhD in computer science, software engineering, data science, computational methods, or a related field, would be ideal.

Preferred Knowledge, Skills, And Abilities

Strong programming skills in Python and the ability to select, adapt, and quickly learn appropriate scientific programming tools and libraries.
Demonstrated ability to design, develop, test, deploy, and maintain complex software systems.
Strong understanding of modular software architecture, API integrations, data architecture, and data modeling.
Ability to rapidly configure reproducible research environments and resolve complex software dependency and installation issues.
Experience with scalable data processing, parallel or distributed execution, and performance optimization.
Working knowledge of research design, statistics, and machine learning sufficient to implement and test computational methods in collaboration with researchers.
Strong code review, debugging, quality control, and documentation skills, with attention to computational accuracy and reproducibility.
Ability to translate evolving research specifications into reusable technical capabilities and communicate feasibility constraints and design tradeoffs clearly.
Ability to plan engineering work, deliver against agreed milestones, and collaborate effectively with researchers and technical colleagues.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience designing, implementing, or evaluating LLM-based or agentic AI systems, including tool integrations, workflow orchestration, and evaluation frameworks.
Experience building reusable infrastructure for large-scale empirical experiments, including configurable pipelines, containerized environments, and reliable execution across computing platforms.
Experience with advanced statistical or machine learning methods, or demonstrated ability to learn and implement such methods quickly.
Experience reading research papers and associated code to support replication, computational validation, and evaluation.
Experience with R or other scientific programming languages in addition to Python.

Experience mentoring developers or research staff and establishing shared practices for software quality, documentation, and reproducible research
