added.description:
Our Purpose

Mastercard powers economies and empowers people in 200+ countries and territories worldwide. Together with our customers, we’re helping build a sustainable economy where everyone can prosper. We support a wide range of digital payments choices, making transactions secure, simple, smart and accessible. Our technology and innovation, partnerships and networks combine to deliver a unique set of products and services that help people, businesses and governments realize their greatest potential.

Title And Summary

Lead AI Engineer

Overview

Mastercard is seeking a Lead AI Engineer to join a small, focused AI technology team led by one of Mastercard's Distinguished Engineers. The team will initially focus on delivering agentic technologies such as the Model Context Protocol (MCP) at scale and the use of open weight AI models. The team works in partnership with key technology stakeholders across the organization.

This is a hands-on engineering role. You will design and build the platform capabilities that let Mastercard adopt MCP and open weight models safely and at scale, working alongside more senior engineers who set the broader technical direction. We are looking for someone with strong knowledge of modern AI technology, solid software engineering and MLOps skills, good cloud platform experience, familiarity with identity technologies such as OAuth and a practical grasp of model evaluation.

In this role, you will help build the platform patterns through which Mastercard teams expose tools and data to agents over MCP, and through which the enterprise services, evaluates, and governs open weight models. You will contribute to the key technical decisions — gateway and connectivity patterns, identity and access controls, model-serving infrastructure, and evaluation — and turn them into working, well-engineered, production-grade services. You will work across the MCP estate and the OW model working group, partnering closely with the team's senior engineers and with central technology, security, and governance stakeholders.

About The Role

Contribute to the design and build of the components of Mastercard's enterprise MCP deployment, such as the security gateway, the MCP registry that governs what exists and who owns it, and reference server implementations that teams build from. Take these from design through to running production services.
Implement the identity, authentication, and authorization patterns for MCP across the estate, working with the team's senior engineers and central security and identity teams so that agents, tools, and data are accessed securely and are auditable end to end.
Help set and apply the standard for internal and external MCP servers — how tools and data are exposed, discovered and versioned, and the inspection, data-protection, rate-limiting, and kill-switch controls the gateway must enforce.
Build and operate open weight model serving — stand up and scale self-hosted inference, package models for deployment, and help enable switching workloads across models and providers for cost, flexibility, and resilience.
Build the evaluation and testing tooling that benchmarks candidate open weight models for quality, cost, latency, and safety, and produces the reproducible evidence that governance and security reviews need.
Apply the MLOps practices that keep the platform reliable — CI/CD, infrastructure-as-code, observability, and model and service monitoring — so that what the team builds is maintainable and operable in production.
Partner with central security, privacy, legal and AI governance teams, and with the MCP SIG and OW working group, implementing their requirements correctly for the platform's architecture.
Keep current with a rapidly evolving landscape, such as new MCP developments, frontier open weight releases, and related agentic protocols, and help the team decide what to adopt, prototype, or wait on.

All About You

Strong knowledge of modern AI technology: LLMs and foundation models, agents, and the tooling and protocols (such as MCP) that connect them to enterprise systems.
Good software engineering skills: you write production-quality, well-tested code and build services others can depend on, not one-off scripts or prototypes.
Solid MLOps experience: CI/CD, infrastructure-as-code, containers, observability, and monitoring for models and services in production.
Good cloud platform knowledge (AWS preferred; Azure or GCP valuable). Familiarity with a modern data/AI platform such as Databricks a bonus.
Practical experience with model evaluation, including building benchmarks and tests that measure quality, cost, latency and safety, and producing reproducible results others can rely on.
Hands-on experience serving or operating open weight models, self-hosting, and scaling inference, and ideally some fine-tuning or adaptation to proprietary data and workflows.
Working knowledge of API security, identity, and access control, enough to implement MCP authentication and authorization correctly and partner effectively with security teams.
Awareness of the governance context that shapes enterprise AI, such as model provenance and licensing, data sovereignty, and financial-services regulation.
A clear communicator and collaborator who works well with senior engineers, hands-on peers, and specialist governance and security partner teams.
Intense curiosity about technology in general, and AI in particular, and who can demonstrate their learning agility outside the bounds of a specific function.
Lastly, a self-starter: once you have a clear guidance and direction, you don’t need to be hand-held to get to a solution or deliverable.

This role is HYBRID in Fairfax, VA requiring you to be in the office Monday, Tuesday and Thursday.

At Apple Federal Credit Union, we’re more than a financial institution; we’re a community-focused organization powered by passionate people. With 24 branches across Northern Virginia and a proud legacy of service, we’re committed to improving the lives of our members and the communities we serve.

We believe our employees are our greatest asset. That’s why we foster a supportive workplace culture that values inclusiveness, innovation and growth. Whether you’re just starting out or advancing your career, you’ll find opportunities for professional development, mentorship and meaningful impact.

Why Work at Apple FCU

Recognized as a USA Top Workplace (2025) and Top Workplace by WTOP (2026)
Collaborative, welcoming environment with forward-thinking leadership
Competitive, comprehensive benefits package, including:
Medical, dental and vision coverage
401(k) with employer match
Paid time off and 11 paid federal holidays
Paid volunteer time to give back
Tuition reimbursement and ongoing training opportunities
Annual TEAM Bonus plan.

Role

Under the general supervision of the Manager, AI & Data Engineering, and in adherence to established policies and procedures, the AI Solutions Engineer II will be responsible for designing, building, and operationalizing AI-powered solutions that transform how staff discover and consume Apple FCU’s enterprise data. This role will serve as a hands-on technical builder who leverages the data platform and curated datasets created by the Data Analytics team to deliver secure, reliable, and scalable AI experiences—such as internal agents that enable staff to ask natural-language questions and receive accurate, explainable answers grounded in governed data.

The AI Solutions Engineer will own key technical decisions and implementations required to make AI usable in production, including AI tooling selection and development, integration patterns, Azure compute/runtime considerations, and end-to-end operational supportability (monitoring, logging, error handling, and deployment discipline). The role will partner closely with Data Engineering, Data Analytics leadership, Cybersecurity/IT stakeholders, and business partners to ensure solutions meet business needs while maintaining appropriate governance, privacy, and security controls.

The candidate will be expected to perform their duties with a mindset that reflects The Apple Way principles: Team Up, Serve with Purpose, Challenge Yourself, and Own It. A keen awareness of and compliance with credit union policies and procedures, as well as regulations pertaining to the Bank Secrecy Act, is imperative. Additionally, the AI Solutions Engineer will undertake other information technology responsibilities as delegated by the Manager, AI & Data Engineering.

Essential Functions & Responsibilities

Build AI-powered data consumption experiences

Design and implement staff-facing AI experiences that allow non-technical users to ask questions in natural language (e.g., “How many members opened accounts yesterday?”) and receive accurate, explainable answers grounded in governed enterprise data.
Implement safe “natural language → analytics” workflows (query planning, schema/metadata grounding, semantic definitions, and response formatting) that prioritize correctness, interpretability, and repeatability.
Ensure AI outputs include the appropriate context (definitions, time windows, filters used, and confidence/limitations) to reduce misinterpretation and improve trust.
Partner with Data Engineering to assess and improve AI-readiness of enterprise datasets, develop metadata, semantic labeling, and data quality standards needed for AI outputs.

Own AI tooling selection, engineering standards, and integrations

Own the technical evaluation, selection, and implementation of AI tooling used to deliver internal AI solutions (model/provider choices, orchestration patterns, retrieval patterns, evaluation harnesses, monitoring/telemetry patterns).
Evaluate and develop agentic AI solutions that will assist in everyday organizational processes, build out multi-step workflows that will act on enterprise data with appropriate oversight and traceability.
Develop reusable “golden path” components that the team can consistently apply: prompt templates, retrieval patterns, tool/function calling patterns, safety/guardrail patterns, logging and tracing, and secure data access adapters.

Partner with Data Engineering to define and maintain the interfaces between the AI consumption layer and the governed data platform (Fabric/Warehouse/Lakehouse), ensuring minimal friction for future AI use cases.

Azure runtime, compute, and operational ownership

Architect and implement the runtime environment for AI services (Azure hosting patterns, identity, secrets, compute scaling, performance tuning, cost controls) to ensure production-grade reliability and supportability.
Implement observability and operational discipline for AI solutions: telemetry, auditing, error handling, incident response hooks, and maintainable runbooks.
Establish release and change discipline for AI solutions (dev/test/prod separation where applicable, automated deployment patterns, rollback approach).

Governance, security, and responsible AI guardrails

Overview

At PNNL, our core capabilities are divided among major departments that we refer to as Directorates within the Lab, focused on a specific area of scientific research or other function, with its own leadership team and dedicated budget.

Our Science & Technology directorates include National Security, Integrated Discovery Sciences, and Energy and Environment. In addition, we have an Environmental Molecular Sciences Laboratory, a Department of Energy, Office of Science user facility housed on the PNNL campus.

The National Security Directorate (NSD) drives science-based, mission-focused solutions to take on complex, real-world threats to our nation and the world.

The AI and Data Analytics Division, part of the National Security Directorate, combines profound domain expertise and creative integration of advanced hardware and software to deliver computational solutions that address complex data and analytic challenges. Working in multidisciplinary teams, we connect foundational research to engineering to operations, providing the tools to innovate quickly and field results faster. Our strengths are integrated across the data analytics lifecycle, from data acquisition and management to analysis and decision support.

Responsibilities

PNNL is seeking a Machine Learning Engineer to implement and adapt research methods within shared software used by U.S. government stakeholders. You will work with researchers in areas such as AI Assurance, agentic AI, and applied mathematics, independently developing and maintaining defined software components within a broader engineering effort.

You will contribute directly to shared codebases, from experimental implementation through deployment primarily in unclassified sponsor environments. The team maintains and improves the software over time. The work focuses on deep learning methods for large language models and computer vision. Projects span research areas such as AI Assurance, agentic AI, and applied mathematics, with opportunities to work with other models and methods.

Key Responsibilities

Implement and adapt deep learning and computational methods with researchers, investigating algorithmic assumptions and debugging implementation and model behavior.
Independently develop, test, and maintain defined software components or features, making design decisions within the broader architecture.
Implement, test, and maintain components of agentic AI workflows, including model tool calling and integration with APIs or data sources, making implementation decisions within the broader software architecture.
Build reusable packages, APIs, and interfaces that connect research methods with sponsor systems and workflows.
Refactor experimental code and improve its clarity, performance, and maintainability.
Develop tests and evaluations that compare implementations with research results and verify behavior as software changes.
Use reproducible environments, dependency management, automated testing, and documentation to support collaborative development.
Work with other engineers to integrate and deploy components, resolve defects, and incorporate research advances and stakeholder feedback.
Coordinate changes in shared codebases, participate in code reviews, and share methods and findings with colleagues.
Share implementation approaches and findings with researchers and engineers working in the broader effort.
Conduct work in secure environments in accordance with operational security requirements.

This position is based in either Richland, WA or Seattle, WA and requires an onsite presence.

Qualifications

Minimum Qualifications:

BS/BA and 2 years of data science experience -OR-
MS/MA -OR-
PhD
Experience using Python with PyTorch, TensorFlow, or a similar deep learning framework.
Experience implementing or adapting methods for large language models, computer vision, or related deep learning applications.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience with modular software design, automated testing, version control, and collaborative development.
Experience building or adapting agentic AI applications, including workflow orchestration, tool integration, or tracing and evaluating multi-step behavior.
Experience interpreting technical literature or mathematical descriptions and collaborating with researchers to implement methods and evaluate results, particularly in AI Assurance, agentic AI, or applied mathematics.
Experience developing reusable packages or APIs and integrating them into larger systems.
Experience deploying and maintaining ML or computational software, including reproducible environments, dependency management, automated build and deployment workflows, and incorporating user feedback.
Experience supporting national security missions.

Hazardous Working Conditions/Environment

Not applicable.

Additional Information

This position requires the ability to obtain and maintain a federal security clearance.

A security clearance background investigation includes review of your employment, education, financial, and criminal history, as well as interviews with you and your personal references, neighbors, and co-workers to determine trustworthiness, reliability, and loyalty to the United States. The investigation also examines your foreign connections, drug and alcohol use, foreign influence, and overall conduct.

Requirements

U.S. Citizenship
Background Investigation: Applicants selected will be subject to a Federal background investigation and must meet eligibility requirements for access to classified matter in accordance with 10 CFR 710, Appendix B.
Drug Testing: All Security Clearance positions are Testing Designated Positions, which means that the applicant selected for hire is subject to pre-employment drug testing, and post-employment random drug testing. In addition, applicants must be able to demonstrate non-use of illegal drugs, including marijuana, for the 12 consecutive months preceding completion of the requisite Questionnaire for National Security Positions (QNSP).

Note: Applicants will be considered ineligible for security clearance processing by the U.S. Department of Energy if non-use of illegal drugs, including marijuana, for 12 months cannot be demonstrated.

Testing Designated Position

Ent Credit Union and Wings Credit Union joined forces in January 2026. This merger means more opportunities, expanded resources, and a shared commitment to delivering exceptional member service. Together, we become more - empowering members, communities, and teams through a bold, unified future. Job Description

This role is responsible for identifying opportunities where artificial intelligence can improve decision making, streamline operations, enhance member experiences, and create measurable business value. It combines business curiosity, experimentation, technical problem solving, and solution development to uncover high value opportunities and transform them into practical, governed AI-enabled solutions. Rather than simply implementing technology, the AI solutions engineer seeks to understand how work gets done today, challenges existing assumptions, and helps business teams discover new and better ways of operating. The successful candidate is comfortable working across business and technical teams, translating operational challenges into innovative solutions while balancing governance, risk management, and long term sustainability. This position owns the full solution lifecycle, from opportunity discovery and requirement definition through solution design, development, testing, deployment, adoption and continuous improvement. Success in this role is measured not by the number of solutions delivered, but by the business outcomes achieved, the problems solved, and the value created for members, employees, and the organization.

Essential Functions

Opportunity Discovery & Experimentation:
Partner with business leaders and subject matter experts to understand workflows, decision processes, operational challenges, and opportunities for improvement.
Identify opportunities where AI can create meaningful business value through increased effectiveness, efficiency, consistency, or member experience.
Form hypotheses, develop rapid prototypes, and conduct experiments to evaluate potential solutions before larger investments are made.
Challenge existing assumptions and recommend alternative approaches when traditional methods no longer represent the best solution.
Employ innovative and evidence-based approaches to solving business problems
Develop business cases and value assessments that support prioritization and investment decisions.

AI Solution Design & Development:
Design, build, test, and implement AI-enabled solutions that improve business outcomes and operational effectiveness.
Develop prototypes, proofs of concept, and production ready solutions using modern AI technologies including generative AI, intelligent automation, machine learning, and workflow orchestration platforms.
Evaluate multiple solution approaches and select the most appropriate technology, methodology, and implementation strategy.
Leverage a broad range of AI tools, platforms and techniques to rapidly iterate and deliver value.
Collaborate with business stakeholders throughout development to validate assumptions and refine solutions.

Business Engagement & Transformation:
Translate business challenges into structured business and technical requirements.
Facilitate discovery sessions to understand current state processes and envision future state operating models.
Help business teams rethink traditional workflows and identify opportunities to create AI-enabled or AI-native processes.
Communicate technical concepts in a clear and business friendly manner.
Manage stakeholder expectations regarding scope, timelines, risk, and anticipated benefits.
Build strong partnerships across business and technical teams to drive adoption and organizational change.

Ensure all AI solutions comply with governance, security, privacy, risk management, and regulatory requirements.
Maintain documentation that supports auditability, transparency, explainability, and long-term sustainability.
Participate in reviews with Risk, Compliance, Information Security, Legal, and Internal Audit partners.
Ensure solutions follow approved change management, model governance, and control frameworks.
Support Responsible AI principles, including fairness, transparency, explainability, accountability, and appropriate human oversight.

Deployment, Adoption & Continuous Improvement:
Collaborate with Data Engineering, Architecture, Infrastructure, and IT teams to deploy solutions into production environments.
Develop testing strategies, implementation plans, deployment documentation, and success metrics.
Monitor solution performance, business outcomes, and adoption.
Continuously refine and improve solutions using stakeholder feedback and performance data.
Create training materials and support organizational adoption efforts.
Facilitate knowledge transfer and long-term sustainability activities.

Innovative & Practice Development:
Contribute to the growth and maturity of the organization's AI capabilities, standards, and methodologies.
Create reusable assets, frameworks, implementation patterns, and best practices.
Share lessons learned and successful approaches across teams.
Actively explore emerging AI technologies, techniques, and business applications.
Serve as a champion for responsible experimentation, innovation, and continuous learning.

Bank Secrecy Act: Remains cognizant of and adheres to Wings policies and procedures, and regulations pertaining to the Bank Secrecy Act.

Equivalent combinations of education, technical training, and demonstrated experience delivering analytical or technology enabled solutions may be considered in lieu of degree requirements

Experience working with AI, automation, or technology-enabled business solutions, required

Ent Credit Union and Wings Credit Union joined forces in January 2026. This merger means more opportunities, expanded resources, and a shared commitment to delivering exceptional member service. Both organizations bring a strong legacy of member satisfaction, operational excellence, financial stability, and community impact. Join us during this transformative time and be part of shaping the future of banking! To learn more about the merger, click here.

Job Description

This role is responsible for identifying opportunities where artificial intelligence can improve decision making, streamline operations, enhance member experiences, and create measurable business value. It combines business curiosity, experimentation, technical problem solving, and solution development to uncover high value opportunities and transform them into practical, governed AI-enabled solutions. Rather than simply implementing technology, the AI solutions engineer seeks to understand how work gets done today, challenges existing assumptions, and helps business teams discover new and better ways of operating. The successful candidate is comfortable working across business and technical teams, translating operational challenges into innovative solutions while balancing governance, risk management, and long term sustainability. This position owns the full solution lifecycle, from opportunity discovery and requirement definition through solution design, development, testing, deployment, adoption and continuous improvement. Success in this role is measured not by the number of solutions delivered, but by the business outcomes achieved, the problems solved, and the value created for members, employees, and the organization.

Essential Functions

Opportunity Discovery & Experimentation:
Partner with business leaders and subject matter experts to understand workflows, decision processes, operational challenges, and opportunities for improvement.
Identify opportunities where AI can create meaningful business value through increased effectiveness, efficiency, consistency, or member experience.
Form hypotheses, develop rapid prototypes, and conduct experiments to evaluate potential solutions before larger investments are made.
Challenge existing assumptions and recommend alternative approaches when traditional methods no longer represent the best solution.
Employ innovative and evidence-based approaches to solving business problems
Develop business cases and value assessments that support prioritization and investment decisions.

AI Solution Design & Development:
Design, build, test, and implement AI-enabled solutions that improve business outcomes and operational effectiveness.
Develop prototypes, proofs of concept, and production ready solutions using modern AI technologies including generative AI, intelligent automation, machine learning, and workflow orchestration platforms.
Evaluate multiple solution approaches and select the most appropriate technology, methodology, and implementation strategy.
Leverage a broad range of AI tools, platforms and techniques to rapidly iterate and deliver value.
Collaborate with business stakeholders throughout development to validate assumptions and refine solutions.

Business Engagement & Transformation:
Translate business challenges into structured business and technical requirements.
Facilitate discovery sessions to understand current state processes and envision future state operating models.
Help business teams rethink traditional workflows and identify opportunities to create AI-enabled or AI-native processes.
Communicate technical concepts in a clear and business friendly manner.
Manage stakeholder expectations regarding scope, timelines, risk, and anticipated benefits.
Build strong partnerships across business and technical teams to drive adoption and organizational change.

Governance, Risk & Responsible AI:
Ensure all AI solutions comply with governance, security, privacy, risk management, and regulatory requirements.
Maintain documentation that supports auditability, transparency, explainability, and long-term sustainability.
Participate in reviews with Risk, Compliance, Information Security, Legal, and Internal Audit partners.
Ensure solutions follow approved change management, model governance, and control frameworks.
Support Responsible AI principles, including fairness, transparency, explainability, accountability, and appropriate human oversight.

Deployment, Adoption & Continuous Improvement:
Collaborate with Data Engineering, Architecture, Infrastructure, and IT teams to deploy solutions into production environments.
Develop testing strategies, implementation plans, deployment documentation, and success metrics.
Monitor solution performance, business outcomes, and adoption.
Continuously refine and improve solutions using stakeholder feedback and performance data.
Create training materials and support organizational adoption efforts.
Facilitate knowledge transfer and long-term sustainability activities.

Innovative & Practice Development:
Contribute to the growth and maturity of the organization's AI capabilities, standards, and methodologies.
Create reusable assets, frameworks, implementation patterns, and best practices.
Share lessons learned and successful approaches across teams.
Actively explore emerging AI technologies, techniques, and business applications.
Serve as a champion for responsible experimentation, innovation, and continuous learning.

Bank Secrecy Act: Remains cognizant of and adheres to Wings policies and procedures, and regulations pertaining to the Bank Secrecy Act.

Qualifications

Minimum Formal Qualifications for this Position:

Master's Degree in a scientific/engineering discipline such as computer science, data science, statistics, mathematics, engineering, artificial intelligence, physics, operations research or a related field, required
Equivalent combinations of education, technical training, and demonstrated experience delivering analytical or technology enabled solutions may be considered in lieu of degree requirements

Experience working with AI, automation, or technology-enabled business solutions, required

Support deployment and troubleshooting in client cloud, on-premises, or hybrid environments. Partner with Implementation Engineers, Data Engineers, and client teams to resolve integration and data-readiness issues.

Gen AI Foundational:

Ability to understand business challenges and translate them into value-add AI solutions leveraging large language models and intelligent automation
Experience designing, building, and maintaining production-grade LLM applications, including end-to-end pipelines from data ingestion through model output delivery (e.g. Azure OpenAI, AWS Bedrock, Google Vertex AI)

Agentic and LLM Ops:

Ability to build reliable agent loops including failure handling, retries, fallbacks, and context window management across complex multi-step agentic workflows
Ability to debug, troubleshoot, and remediate production LLM and agentic systems including failure diagnosis across retrieval, orchestration, and generation layers
Experience designing and implementing LLM evaluation frameworks covering functional correctness, output quality, safety, and business-defined KPIs (e.g. RAGAS, DeepEval, ArizePhoenix etc.)

Software Engineering:

Hands-on software engineering proficiency in Python, with the ability to write clean, modular, production-quality code for LLM pipelines and agentic applications
Experience working with structured and unstructured data sets to support LLM application development, including data curation, preparation, and quality validation for model inputs
Familiarity with RESTful and event-driven API patterns including asynchronous workflows, service boundaries, and integration of enterprise data sources to expose LLM and agentic capabilities
Familiarity with containerization and orchestration concepts for packaging and deploying LLM applications in cloud environments (e.g. Docker, Kubernetes, Azure Container Apps, AWS ECS etc.)
Understanding of software engineering best practices as applied to ML systems, including modular code design, testing patterns for AI pipelines, and data quality validation

Clear communicator able to explain complex AI system behavior and tradeoffs to technical and nontechnical stakeholders, including risk and compliance.
Strong ownership and accountability, taking responsibility for AI systems from design through production and issue resolution.

Collaborative and cross functional, working closely with engineering, product, risk, legal, and audit teams.

Ability to build and maintain model observability pipelines including tracing of multi-step agentic reasoning chains, output degradation detection, and behavioral drift monitoring in production (e.g. LangSmith, Arize, Datadog, Azure Monitor etc.)
Familiarity with LLM fine-tuning approaches including instruction tuning and preference optimization, with an understanding of when fine-tuning is appropriate versus prompt-based solutions (e.g. LoRA, QLoRA, PEFT, NeMo Framework etc.)

Familiarity with AI-assisted software engineering tools for accelerating development, implementation, and code review practices (e.g. Claude Code, GitHub Copilot, Codex etc.)

Prior consulting experience

added.title: Senior Software Engineer- AI Agents & Integration
added.description:
Job Type

Full-time

Description

At First Electronic Bank (FEB), we are driven by the purpose to make credit accessible to everyday Americans and their businesses. Partnering with some of the most innovative fintech companies in the nation, we offer a wide range of consumer and commercial credit and deposit products on a national basis. Offering deposit accounts and debit cards, revolving lines of credit, private-label credit cards, installment financing programs and more, FEB engages with strategic, collaborative partners, promoting services and products to provide the most beneficial consumer and commercial financing solutions.

First Electronic Bank (FEB) is seeking a highly capable software engineer to independently lead ambiguous, high-impact initiatives that deliver FEB's internal applications, secure APIs and services, fintech integrations, and agent-based capabilities from problem definition through measurable production outcomes. We're looking for a senior engineer who builds real business applications, connects systems through APIs, and uses AI agents as a practical part of delivering software. This is not an AI research or prompt engineering role. Instead, we're seeking a hands-on builder who knows how to leverage AI to accelerate development while applying sound engineering judgment to validate outputs, manage context and handoffs, and ensure production-quality results.

In this role, you will build polished user interfaces and robust backend services that connect enterprise systems and orchestrate workflows across approved MCP servers. You'll own application design, development, release readiness, and operational outcomes while working within Engineering and Infrastructure standards and the bank's cloud control framework. You will also help transform successful solutions into reusable patterns, frameworks, and best practices for the broader team. This role is ideal for an experienced engineer who combines strong software engineering fundamentals with a pragmatic approach to AI-assisted development in production environments.

Representative work: Build and enhance internal applications with production-quality front-end and backend services; integrate fintech and enterprise platforms through secure APIs; prototype targeted AI-enabled workflows; and develop an extensible tool-routing layer that supports multiple approved MCP servers.

What You'll Do

Own complex application workstreams end to end: clarify the problem and success measures; design secure APIs, services, and data exchanges within established architecture; manage dependencies and risk; and drive delivery through adoption, production support, troubleshooting, and proactive improvement.
Production accountability: Own application reliability, operational readiness, runbooks, model usage, and post-release remediation; partner with Infrastructure on environments, CI/CD guardrails, identity, networking, secrets, observability, capacity, incidents, and cloud costs.
Agent workflows: Provide authoritative context, manage task state and handoffs, and configure multi-step workflows with sequencing, branching, retries, checkpoints, tracing, and approvals; route work to approved MCP servers and tools based on task and permissions.
Agentic coding: Use GitHub Copilot or comparable coding agents to delegate work, supply repository context, review generated changes, and retain human ownership of quality, security, and release decisions.
Verification and controls: Use tests, end-to-end verification, security review, evaluations, and monitoring; enforce sensitive-data handling, least privilege, audit evidence, rollback, and human approval before consequential actions.
Applied prototyping: Periodically work with business users to prototype internal applications and workflows using approved data and tools, then retire, control, or productionize them based on value and risk.
Partner across business, product, security, compliance, and Infrastructure; mentor through design and code reviews; and convert proven approaches into reusable components, templates, and playbooks that improve delivery across the team.

Requirements

What We're Looking For:

5+ years of software engineering experience (or equivalent scope) delivering production applications across interfaces, APIs, and integrations.
Demonstrated success independently leading ambiguous, high-impact work from problem definition through sustained production use and measurable results, while mentoring engineers and improving team practices.
Strong JavaScript or TypeScript and a modern web framework, plus proficiency in C#/.NET, Python, or Java for backend services, APIs, and integrations.
Understanding of RESTful API and service design, OAuth2/OIDC, OpenAPI/Swagger, secure data exchange, and integration patterns for reliable distributed applications.
Experience building cloud-hosted applications on Azure, AWS, or Google Cloud and partnering with Infrastructure on CI/CD, environment controls, security, monitoring, scaling, incident response, and cost management.
Demonstrable use of GitHub Copilot, Claude Code, Codex, or comparable tools to coordinate agents, manage context and handoffs, verify changes, and deliver tested software; familiarity connecting agents to tools or MCP servers is expected, but building a custom platform is not.
Practical knowledge of agent state, prompt-injection and data-leakage risks, least privilege, secrets, auditability, and recovery.
Ability to turn an ambiguous business problem into a focused prototype and explain tradeoffs to non-technical users.
Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, Information Technology, or a related field.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience deploying applications or integrations in banking, fintech, payments, or another regulated environment; Federal Reserve payment, settlement, or reporting APIs are especially valuable.
Cloud data and messaging services such as Fabric, Service Bus, Kafka, or equivalent.
Microsoft 365 Copilot, Copilot Studio, Power Platform, or comparable enterprise automation tools.
Managed AI/agent platforms such as Microsoft Foundry, Amazon Bedrock, or Google Cloud Vertex AI, including deployment, evaluation, and tracing.
Experience building or integrating MCP servers, tool registries, or multi-server routing layers, and turning that work into reusable patterns adopted by other engineers or teams; Go, Python, TypeScript, or C#/.NET experience is valuable.
Master’s degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, Information Technology, or a related field.

added.title: Defense Innovation Research Engineer
added.description:
Job Overview:

PatchPlus Consulting (PPC), through its technology division PatchPlus Technologies (P2T), is seeking a highly motivated Defense Innovation Research Software Engineer
to support Department of War (DoW) research, development, prototyping, and capability development efforts. The successful candidate will contribute directly to the design, development, integration, testing, and deployment of software solutions supporting advanced defense technologies and mission-focused applications.

This position is ideal for a junior-to-mid-level Software Engineer with experience using AI to support software development and who is comfortable working with frontier AI tools and techniques, including AI coding assistants and agentic development workflows. The successful candidate will enjoy bringing an AI-native development mindset to solving technical challenges, collaborating with multidisciplinary engineering teams, and applying these tools to develop, test, and refine software that advances research concepts into operational prototypes, while strictly adhering to project security and data-handling boundaries. Projects may support autonomy, AI/ML, cyber operations, electronic warfare, command and control, mission systems, data analytics, digital engineering, cloud-based platforms, and emerging defense technologies.

The Engineer will collaborate closely with software developers, systems engineers, military subject matter experts, data scientists, and researchers to build scalable, secure, and mission-focused solutions for government customers. Responsibilities include software design, coding, testing, integration, troubleshooting, and technical documentation throughout the software development lifecycle.

Previous experience supporting DoW research and development efforts, including Small Business Innovation Research (SBIR), Small Business Technology Transfer (STTR), Other Transaction Authority (OTA) projects, rapid prototyping, experimentation, or defense technology development is highly desirable.
This position primarily supports remote work with periodic travel for customer engagements, integration events, technical exchanges, demonstrations, testing activities, and team collaboration within the United States.

The ideal candidate will demonstrate traits that align with PatchPlus' guiding principles— Purpose, Proficiency, and Character
. PatchPlus' purpose is to continue making a difference to our nation's security while providing meaningful employment to its owner-employees. Proficiency reflects our commitment to technical excellence, innovation, and continuous learning. Character reflects the integrity, accountability, and professionalism expected of every team member.

Responsibilities/Duties
:
Design, develop, test, deploy, and maintain software applications supporting DoW research, development, and prototyping efforts.
Identify, evaluate, integrate, and employ frontier AI tools and techniques—including secure self-hosted/local AI coding assistants, agentic workflows, and open-weights models —to support user stories, coding, testing, debugging, documentation, and development efficiency.
Review, sandbox, and validate AI-generated code and other outputs for correctness, security, and maintainability, using tools consistent with project requirements and data-handling restrictions, and security protocols.
• Apply context engineering and specification-driven development to structure codebases and prompts for optimal AI agent reasoning, maximizing output accuracy while minimizing technical debt.
Develop APIs, backend services, web applications, data pipelines, and cloud-based solutions.
Apply secure coding practices and perform software integration, debugging, troubleshooting, performance tuning, and testing.
Collaborate with engineers, researchers, and military subject matter experts to develop mission-focused capabilities.
Participate in Agile development activities, technical documentation, and configuration management throughout the software development lifecycle.
Contribute to proof-of-concept efforts, prototype demonstrations, and technology transition activities.

Requirements
:
U.S. citizenship and the ability to obtain and maintain a Secret security clearance.
Bachelor’s degree in computer science, Software Engineering, Computer Engineering, Information Systems, or a related field.
Software development experience appropriate to the position level: junior-level candidates may demonstrate experience through internships, academic projects, or relevant personal projects; mid-level candidates should have approximately 4–6 years of relevant professional experience.
Proficiency in one or more modern programming languages, such as Python, Java, JavaScript/TypeScript, C++, C#, or Go.
Hands-on experience developing software applications, APIs, or backend services.
Experience using AI tools to support software development, including code generation, debugging, testing, or documentation.
Familiarity with frontier AI tools and techniques—including AI coding assistants, large language models, and agentic development workflows—and the ability to review and validate AI-generated outputs for correctness, security, and maintainability.
Understanding of software engineering fundamentals, including software design, secure coding practices, debugging, and testing.
Familiarity with relational or NoSQL databases, such as SQL-based databases or MongoDB.
Experience using Git or a comparable version-control system and familiarity with collaborative development workflows.
Familiarity with cloud platforms, containerization, and continuous integration/continuous delivery (CI/CD) concepts.
Strong problem-solving, communication, and collaboration skills, with a willingness to learn new tools and technologies.
Willingness to travel up to 15% for customer meetings, technical exchanges, integration and testing events, and team collaboration.

Preferred Qualifications:

Active Secret or Top Secret security clearance.
Experience supporting DoD, Intelligence Community, or other federal government software development programs.
Experience applying advanced AI-assisted development techniques, such as configuring coding agents, integrating AI tools into development workflows, or providing project-specific context to improve AI-generated outputs.
Experience with Azure DevOps, CI/CD pipelines, automated testing, or DevOps/DevSecOps practices.
Experience with cloud platforms such as AWS, Azure, or Google Cloud, and container technologies such as Docker or Kubernetes.
Experience with software architecture and design, particularly for mid-level candidates.

Experience working in classified or sensitive government environments.

added.description:
Senior Conversational AI Engineer (Voice AI / IVR)

Remote

Compensation: $70 - $80/hr W2

Employment Type: Long-Term Contract (12+ months)

About The Role

Brooksource is seeking an experienced Senior Conversational AI Engineer to lead the development, enhancement, and ongoing maintenance of an enterprise-level automated voice agent platform. In this long-term remote contract role, you will take hands-on technical ownership of established conversational AI solutions leveraging Cognigy.AI, NICE CXone, and integrated backend systems. You will play a critical role in maintaining production stability, troubleshooting complex integrations, enhancing existing functionality, and developing new capabilities to improve customer experience and operational efficiency. The ideal candidate combines deep expertise in conversational AI development, IVR engineering, software development, and API integration, and is comfortable working within established production environments, independently diagnosing technical issues, writing and modifying code, and taking ownership of complex applications. Success in this role requires a holistic understanding of how conversational AI, contact center systems, APIs, and backend applications work together to deliver scalable, reliable solutions.

What You'll Do

Own the development, configuration, administration, maintenance, and production support of enterprise conversational AI and voice agent solutions
Design, develop, test, and deploy conversational AI workflows, voice bot interactions, IVR scripts, prompts, and call-routing logic
Enhance AI-powered virtual agent capabilities, including LLM integrations, natural language understanding (NLU), knowledge management, and conversation context handling
Build, maintain, and troubleshoot RESTful APIs, webhooks, authentication mechanisms (including OAuth 2.0), and integrations between conversational AI platforms, contact center technologies, and enterprise systems
Write, debug, and maintain code using JavaScript, TypeScript, Python, SQL, and related technologies
Diagnose and resolve production issues involving conversational flows, API connectivity, call routing, system performance, and voice integrations
Participate in technical knowledge transfer, reviewing existing architecture, configurations, integrations, and development practices
Establish and maintain technical documentation, development standards, troubleshooting procedures, and ongoing maintenance processes
Monitor automated agent performance, analyze call outcomes and system logs, and identify opportunities to improve reliability, customer experience, and operational efficiency
Support regression testing, release management, deployments, and rollback procedures to maintain platform stability
Collaborate with technical teams, business stakeholders, and external partners to translate business needs into scalable conversational AI solutions
Support the transition of application ownership from third-party vendors to internal teams as needed
Optimize conversational AI performance, call containment, customer experience, and automated resolution rates

Overview

At PNNL, our core capabilities are divided among major departments that we refer to as Directorates within the Lab, focused on a specific area of scientific research or other function, with its own leadership team and dedicated budget.

Our Science & Technology directorates include National Security, Integrated Discovery Sciences, and Energy and Environment. In addition, we have an Environmental Molecular Sciences Laboratory, a Department of Energy, Office of Science user facility housed on the PNNL campus.

The National Security Directorate (NSD) drives science-based, mission-focused solutions to take on complex, real-world threats to our nation and the world.

The AI and Data Analytics Division, part of the National Security Directorate, combines profound domain expertise and creative integration of advanced hardware and software to deliver computational solutions that address complex data and analytic challenges. Working in multidisciplinary teams, we connect foundational research to engineering to operations, providing the tools to innovate quickly and field results faster. Our strengths are integrated across the data analytics lifecycle, from data acquisition and management to analysis and decision support.

Responsibilities

PNNL is seeking a Lead Machine Learning Engineer to lead the development and evolution of software that brings emerging research methods into sponsor environments. You will work with researchers, engineers, and U.S. government stakeholders to shape technical approaches, resolve difficult implementation and integration challenges, and guide shared software through deployment and continued improvement.

You will contribute directly to shared codebases, from experimental implementation through deployment primarily in unclassified sponsor environments. The team maintains and improves the software over time. The work focuses on deep learning methods for large language models and computer vision. Projects span research areas such as AI Assurance, agentic AI, and applied mathematics, with opportunities to work with other models and methods.

You will lead through project teams, remain hands-on in technical work, and help engineers grow through mentoring, feedback, and opportunities to take on greater responsibility.

Key Responsibilities

Set architecture and engineering direction for complex software capabilities involving multiple components, contributors, and stakeholder needs.
Guide the architecture and implementation of agentic AI systems across shared codebases, working with researchers and engineers to resolve tradeoffs involving model and tool integration, workflow orchestration, reliability, and sponsor deployment constraints.
Work with researchers to interpret and adapt emerging methods, resolving difficult tradeoffs among research intent, implementation behavior, performance, and deployment constraints.
Contribute directly to consequential implementation and debugging work, including deep learning methods in PyTorch.
Lead software evolution through development, deployment, and continued maintenance, coordinating technical plans, dependencies, and contributions across project teams.
Align interfaces and implementation approaches across shared codebases with researchers, engineers, and U.S. government stakeholders.
Guide testing and evaluation approaches that verify algorithmic behavior, integration, and reliability as methods and software change.
Guide reproducible development and release practices, including dependency management, automated testing, documentation, and compatibility across components.
Develop engineers through design discussions, code reviews, sustained mentoring, and opportunities to take on greater responsibility.
Shape technical plans and contribute to proposals with collaborators to support continued software development and new capabilities.
Conduct work in secure environments in accordance with operational security requirements.

This position is based in either Richland, WA or Seattle, WA and requires an onsite presence.

Qualifications

Minimum Qualifications:

BS/BA and 7+ years of data science experience -OR-
MS/MA and 5+ years of data science experience -OR-
PhD with 3+ years of data science experience.
Experience using Python with PyTorch, TensorFlow, or a similar deep learning framework.
Experience implementing or adapting methods for large language models, computer vision, or related deep learning applications.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience leading software architecture, design, and implementation across multiple components and stakeholders, including guiding technical decisions and mentoring engineers.
Experience leading the development and evolution of agentic AI systems, including reusable components, evaluation, observability, and deployment across multiple contributors or projects.
Experience interpreting technical literature or mathematical descriptions, discussing assumptions with researchers, and implementing, adapting, or debugging methods for research and deployment, particularly in AI Assurance, agentic AI, or applied mathematics.
Experience maintaining and evolving shared software, including managing interfaces, dependencies, and integration changes, with practices for testing, reproducible development, code review, and releases.
Experience coordinating software development across organizations or with U.S. government stakeholders, deploying and improving software in sponsor environments, or developing technical plans and proposals for research or software development.
Experience supporting national security missions.

Hazardous Working Conditions/Environment

Not applicable.

Additional Information

This position requires the ability to obtain and maintain a federal security clearance.

A security clearance background investigation includes review of your employment, education, financial, and criminal history, as well as interviews with you and your personal references, neighbors, and co-workers to determine trustworthiness, reliability, and loyalty to the United States. The investigation also examines your foreign connections, drug and alcohol use, foreign influence, and overall conduct.

Requirements

U.S. Citizenship
Background Investigation: Applicants selected will be subject to a Federal background investigation and must meet eligibility requirements for access to classified matter in accordance with 10 CFR 710, Appendix B.
Drug Testing: All Security Clearance positions are Testing Designated Positions, which means that the applicant selected for hire is subject to pre-employment drug testing, and post-employment random drug testing. In addition, applicants must be able to demonstrate non-use of illegal drugs, including marijuana, for the 12 consecutive months preceding completion of the requisite Questionnaire for National Security Positions (QNSP).

Note: Applicants will be considered ineligible for security clearance processing by the U.S. Department of Energy if non-use of illegal drugs, including marijuana, for 12 months cannot be demonstrated.eferral Eligible”

Testing Designated Position

This position is a Testing Designated Position (TDP). The candidate selected for this position will be subject to pre-employment and random drug testing for illegal drugs, including marijuana, consistent with the Controlled Substances Act and the PNNL Workplace Substance Abuse Program.

About PNNL

Pacific Northwest National Laboratory (PNNL) is a world-class research institution powered by a highly educated, diverse workforce committed to the values of Integrity, Creativity, Collaboration, Impact, and Courage. Every year, scores of dynamic, driven people come to PNNL to work with renowned researchers on meaningful science, innovations and outcomes for the U.S. Department of Energy and other sponsors; here is your chance to be one of them!

At PNNL, you will find an exciting research environment and excellent benefits including health insurance, and flexible work schedules. PNNL is located in eastern Washington State—the dry side of Washington known for its stellar outdoor recreation and affordable cost of living. The Lab’s campus is only a 45-minute flight (or ~3 hour drive) from Seattle or Portland, and is serviced by the convenient PSC airport, connected to 8 major hubs.

Commitment to Excellence and Equal Employment Opportunity

Our laboratory is committed to fostering a work environment where all individuals are treated with fairness and respect while solving critical challenges in fundamental sciences, national security, and energy resiliency. We are an Equal Employment Opportunity employer.

Pacific Northwest National Laboratory (PNNL) is an Equal Opportunity Employer. PNNL considers all applicants for employment without regard to race, religion, color, sex, national origin, age, disability, genetic information (including family medical history), protected veteran status, and any other status or characteristic protected by federal, state, and/or local laws.

We are committed to providing reasonable accommodations for individuals with disabilities and disabled veterans in our job application procedures and in employment. If you need assistance or an accommodation due to a disability, contact us at careers@pnnl.gov.

Drug Free Workplace

PNNL is committed to a drug-free workplace supported by Workplace Substance Abuse Program (WSAP) and complies with federal laws prohibiting the possession and use of illegal drugs.

If you are offered employment at PNNL, you must pass a drug test prior to commencing employment. PNNL complies with federal law regarding illegal drug use. Under federal law, marijuana remains an illegal drug. If you test positive for any illegal controlled substance, including marijuana, your offer of employment will be withdrawn.

Security, Credentialing, And Eligibility Requirements

As a national laboratory, PNNL is responsible for adhering to the Homeland Security Presidential Directive 12 (HSPD-12) and Department of Energy (DOE) Order 473.1A, which require new employees to obtain and maintain a HSPD-12 Personal Identify Verification (PIV) Credential. To obtain this credential, new employees must successfully complete the applicable tier of federal background investigation post hire and receive a favorable federal adjudication. The tier of federal background investigation will be determined by job duties and national security or public trust responsibilities associated with the job. All tiers of investigation include a declaration of illegal drug activities, including use, supply, possession, or manufacture within the last 1 to 7 years (depending on the applicable tier of investigation). Illegal drug activities include marijuana and cannabis derivatives, which are still considered illegal under federal law, regardless of state laws.

For Foreign National Candidates

If you have not resided in the U.S. for three consecutive years, you are not eligible for the PIV credential and instead will need to obtain a favorable Local Site Specific Only (LSSO) Federal risk determination to maintain employment. Once you meet the three-year residency requirement thereafter, you will be required to obtain a PIV credential to maintain employment. The tier of federal background investigation required to obtain the PIV credential will be determined by job duties at the time you become eligible for the PIV credential.

Mandatory Requirements

Please be aware that the Department of Energy (DOE) prohibits DOE employees and contractors from having any affiliation with the foreign government of a country DOE has identified as a “country of risk” without explicit approval by DOE and Battelle. If you are offered a position at PNNL and currently have any affiliation with the government of one of these countries, you will be required to disclose this information and recuse yourself of that affiliation or receive approval from DOE and Battelle prior to your first day of employment.

Job Summary

The future is bright for the Porch Group, and we'd love for you to be a part of it as our Senior Platform Engineer - AI Platform
.

ISN is hiring a Senior Platform Engineer to lead AI-first platform work at the intersection of agentic systems and production infrastructure. You'll design and ship the systems that let agents and LLMs do real work inside a high-volume product — spanning scheduling, report intake, customer communication, billing workflows, and data extraction. You'll also own the foundation underneath it: our PHP application, AWS/ECS infrastructure, and MySQL/Aurora data layer. Build AI features end to end — retrieval, context engineering, structured output, tool/function calling, and evaluation harnesses that measure whether a change actually made things better
Design and operate agent orchestration systems — multi-agent and multi-step workflows including task decomposition, tool routing, state and memory, retries and fallbacks, human-in-the-loop checkpoints, and guardrails against failure modes that don't look like exceptions

Raise the bar across the team through code review, design docs, mentorship, incident response, and on-call participation

10+ years building and running production software, with real ownership of systems at scale
Demonstrated, hands-on experience shipping LLM-backed features — not just API calls, but agent orchestration, RAG, evaluation, and the operational discipline to keep them working

Nice to have: Go, MCP or comparable agent-tooling standards, vector search and embedding pipelines, Kubernetes, document and image extraction pipelines, or real estate/proptech/field-services domain experience

added.title: Staff Software Engineer, Agentic Analytics
added.description:
Who are we?

Cohere is the leading security-first enterprise AI company. We build cutting-edge foundation AI models and end-to-end products that are designed to solve real-world business problems.

We’re training and deploying frontier models for enterprises who are building AI systems. We believe that our work is instrumental to the widespread adoption of AI and we are looking for folks that want to be part of that.

We obsess over what we build. Each one of us is responsible for contributing to increasing the capabilities of our models and the value they drive for our customers. Cohere is a team of researchers, engineers, designers, and more, who are all passionate about their craft.

We are a global technology company headquartered in Toronto with key offices in London, New York City, San Francisco, Montreal, Paris, Berlin and Seoul. Join us!

Why this role?

We're building the foundational infrastructure that will define how the world thinks about and deploys AI, and we want the sharpest, most driven, and most curious people to help us do it. As the founding lead of Agentic Analytics, a new team in our Analytics and Data Insights organization, you'll own how Cohere gets answers from its own data: an agentic analytics system that answers business questions over governed data, shows the source, query, and freshness behind every answer, and asks for clarification or declines when the evidence is insufficient.

Agentic analytics is far from a solved problem, and correctness is the hard part. A query that runs can still answer the wrong question. Agents go wrong when a business term maps to more than one table, when data goes stale, and when the right context never reaches the model. The worst failures are silent and plausible: a join that double-counts, a wrong denominator, missing data read as zero. Getting this right takes governed definitions, context an agent can use, and an evaluation bar that decides what ships.

You'll build on work already in motion: an internal analytics agent in pilot on our BigQuery warehouse, which is fed by tested ingestion pipelines and modeled in dbt. In your first year, you'll take it to production for teams across Cohere, one domain at a time, and make it replicable: each new domain stands up with configuration, a fresh evaluation set, and very little new code.

This is a hands-on staff engineering role reporting to our Senior Director of Data Analytics. You'll write production code and evaluation sets yourself while managing a small founding team that grows as the system proves itself. You may have held the title software engineer, AI engineer, or data scientist; what matters is that you've built a system like this and run it in production.

Responsibilities

As the lead of Agentic Analytics, you will:

Own the system end to end. Set the architecture for how a business question becomes a governed query and a verifiable answer: interpreting the question, retrieving the right context, applying approved definitions and joins, enforcing the asking user's permissions, and attaching the evidence (source, query, freshness) to every answer.
Build and run it in production. Design the core services and write much of the first version yourself: agent-facing data tools (MCP or equivalent), context retrieval, agent skills for analytics, and the APIs that serve answers. Hold them to production standards for reliability, latency, cost, security, and observability. Put it where people already work: Slack, North, IDEs, and other agents.
Hold every release to the evaluation bar. Build and run the evaluation harness, and define what correct means in each domain: ground-truth question sets, including held-out cases and questions the agent should clarify or decline; result-level scoring, correct-or-decline rates, coverage, and error severity; and regression tests on every change to context, skills, or models. Nothing ships below the bar, and the call on when a domain is ready for production is yours.
Engineer the context layer. Turn metric definitions, approved joins, documentation generated from the code that builds each table, a business glossary, and worked examples into context the agent can use. Every correction becomes a reviewed definition and a regression test.
Roll it out across Cohere. Bring domains such as marketing, revenue, finance, and product onto the system one at a time, each with named owners, certified definitions, and its own evaluation set. Measure adoption, accuracy, turnaround, and correction effort against how those teams work today.
Make it replicable. Package the tools, skills, context templates, and evaluations, and document them well enough that other teams at Cohere can run the system without you.
Hire and lead the team. Bring on the team's first engineers, set the technical bar, review the work, and develop the people doing it.
Partner across Cohere. Work with our data platform team on the warehouse and semantic models, our model evaluation team on evaluation methodology, our security team on access, and each domain's owners on definitions and rollout.

Qualifications

You may be a good fit, if you have:

10+ years building and operating production analytics or software systems, including technical leadership of a team or of systems that span teams
Experience shipping LLM agents to production: tool use, MCP or similar, retrieval and context engineering, guardrails, and observability, with firm opinions on where they fail
Hands-on experience building natural-language or agentic analytics (text-to-SQL, analytics agents, question answering over a semantic layer) that real users relied on, and evidence that it was right
Depth in evaluating LLM systems: golden sets, result-level comparison, abstention metrics, error taxonomies, and regression testing in CI, plus the judgment to tell a good demo from a system you'd put in front of a CFO
Strong Python and SQL, and experience designing and running production services and APIs on a major cloud (Google Cloud is a plus)
Fluency with data: cloud warehouses (BigQuery, Snowflake, or similar), dbt, and semantic layers (MetricFlow, LookML, Cube, or similar). You think in grain, metric definitions, and approved joins, and you can tell when a number is wrong before it reaches a decision
Experience building identity-aware access for agents, where the agent acts with the asking user's permissions and every query leaves an audit trail
Experience hiring and developing engineers, with a leadership style grounded in empathy as much as in data
Genuine excitement about AI: you follow the research, have opinions, and enjoy being in the weeds
Comfort operating in ambiguity, leading through partners you don't manage, and writing design docs and eval reports that settle decisions across teams

If some of the above doesn't line up perfectly with your experience, we still encourage you to apply!

Full-Time Employees At Cohere Enjoy These Perks

A weekly lunch stipend of $75/£75 or equivalent in your local currency for lunch.
Full health and dental benefits, including a separate budget for mental health.
RRSP matching, 401K, Pension Scheme.
100% Parental Leave top-up for up to 6 months, for either parent.
Annual enrichment benefits:

Arts & culture, fitness/wellness, quality time, and a workspace improvement credit.

Education & learning stipend for conferences, courses, and coaching.

6 weeks of paid vacation (30 working days!)
Budget for traveling to other offices if you are remote, plus an annual company offsite.

How And Where We Work

Cohere is remote-friendly, but we also have offices in Toronto, London, New York City, San Francisco, Montreal, Paris, Berlin and Seoul with more opening soon.
For those in the office: a daily lunch program, plenty of snacks, and regular community and social events.
For those not near an office: a co-working benefit so you can work alongside others in your city.
Everyone receives a $500 home office stipend to set up your workspace properly.

If any of the above doesn’t line up exactly with your experience, we still encourage you to apply.

We strive to create an inclusive work environment for all; we welcome applicants from all backgrounds and are committed to providing equal opportunities. Should you require any accommodations during the recruitment process, please submit an Accommodations Request Form, and we will work together to meet your needs.

We may use AI-enabled tools to screen and assess applicants against the criteria for this position. This helps our recruiters identify potentially qualified candidates, but it doesn't limit the applications our recruiters may review or consider.

All legitimate roles are listed on the Cohere careers page and LinkedIn only, with all communications from Cohere employees coming from an @cohere.com or @cw.cohere email alias. If jobs are viewed on other sites then please verify these through our official careers page.

About The Role

As a Senior Software Engineer, you will help build the next phase of this transformation. You will deliver the APIs, Angular experiences, and AI-enabled workflows behind customer self-service, License Intelligence, reporting, and integrations. You are a hands-on engineer who enjoys modernization and scale challenges. You will own your deliverables end to end and use AI tools and agentic patterns responsibly to raise the team's productivity.

About Business License

Business License helps organizations manage the complexity of business licensing and regulatory compliance across jurisdictions. Our solutions support license research, ordering, renewals, workflow, documentation, reporting, and ongoing compliance operations. Business License has impressive and consistent double-digit growth and an aggressive multi-year plan to continue to speed things up.

We are modernizing a mature product portfolio into a scalable, cloud-based ecosystem. Recent progress includes migration to Wolters Kluwer cloud infrastructure, conversion of a large Silverlight desktop application to Angular, improved release automation and resilience, and creation of the foundation for a License Intelligence Platform. The next phase focuses on platform simplification, service decoupling, enterprise performance, customer self-service, integrations, and AI-enabled workflows.

Responsibilities

Design, develop, test, and maintain scalable applications using .NET Framework/.NET, ASP.NET (MVC, Web API, Web Forms) and Angular (v18+) with NgRx.
Build, enhance, and integrate RESTful APIs, with secure design, documentation, and API testing.
Contribute to decoupling legacy, tightly coupled applications into modular services and modern APIs.
Design and build agentic workflows (tool use, multi-step reasoning, structured outputs) and integrate LLM capabilities into applications.
Validate and review AI-generated code against team standards.
Write unit tests (NUnit, Jasmine) and maintain code coverage and testing routines.
Deploy and host applications in IIS, self-hosted, and Azure environments. Use Azure DevOps and CI/CD pipelines.
Monitor application health with New Relic and Datadog. Troubleshoot and resolve production issues.
Identify bottlenecks and optimize performance.
Write technical specifications and design documentation.
Collaborate with cross-functional teams in an Agile/Scrum environment and communicate progress and risks clearly.
Prepare and preprocess data for application use. Support end users with maintenance and troubleshooting.
Contribute to solution design and mentor peers informally.

Required Qualifications

5+ years in .NET and Angular development. 1+ year of agentic AI development.
Bachelor’s degree in computer science, software engineering, engineering, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience. Master’s degree is a plus.
Strong experience in C#, ASP.NET, REST API design, SQL Server and SSRS, and relational database design.
Experience with GitHub, version control, branching/merging, and Azure DevOps CI/CD.
Working knowledge of Azure services.
Experience with AI coding tools such as GitHub Copilot, including output validation and responsible-use practices.
Strong problem-solving, analytical, and testing skills.
Ownership and accountability, and the ability to work with minimal supervision.

Preferred Qualifications

Python proficiency (or similar scripting language) for AI/agent development.
LLM fundamentals: inference, context limits, cost/latency tradeoffs.
Prompting patterns such as ReAct and Chain-of-Thought.
Agentic RAG, vector databases, and embeddings.
LangChain, AutoGen, CrewAI, or similar frameworks. Multi-agent orchestration.
Experience evaluating models, mitigating hallucinations, and designing safe action loops.
OAuth/OIDC, Oracle Database, and legacy modernization experience.
TensorFlow/PyTorch familiarity.

Our Interview Practices

To maintain a fair and genuine hiring process, we kindly ask that all candidates participate in interviews without the assistance of AI tools or external prompts. Our interview process is designed to assess your individual skills, experiences, and communication style. We value authenticity and want to ensure we’re getting to know you—not a digital assistant. To help maintain this integrity, we ask to remove virtual backgrounds and include in-person interviews in our hiring process. Please note that use of AI-generated responses or third-party support during interviews will be grounds for disqualification from the recruitment process.

Applicants may be required to appear onsite at a Wolters Kluwer office as part of the recruitment process.

Expert knowledge of data engineering frameworks, technologies, tools, processes, patterns, and procedures, including how they impact and integrate with other technology areas such as Architecture or Infrastructure
Performs highly complex technical tasks independently
Expert knowledge of TD applications, systems, networks, innovation, design activities, business, organization, best practices, and standards

Recognized as primary subject matter expert in multiple areas directly and indirectly related to key accountabilities
Consults with peers and partners across multiple teams on all aspects of research, analysis, design, and support

Graduate Degree preferred
5+ years of relevant experience

Strong hands-on data engineering experience with Azure and Databricks.
Advanced proficiency in Python, SQL, Spark/PySpark.
Understanding of batch, streaming, dimensional modeling, Lakehouse architecture, and distributed processing.
Hands-on experience developing GenAI or agentic applications.
Experience with Databricks Genie, AI/BI, MLflow, vector search, RAG, or comparable technologies.
Experience engineering data for AI/ML workloads.
Experience within financial services or another highly regulated industry.

Customer Accountabilities

Performs data analysis and assesses data management requirements for a specific Platform or Journey, including complex analysis involving multiple pods or products
Maintains expert knowledge of upstream data, including knowledge provided through data profiling, data quality reporting, and via the production of metadata
Supports the acquisition and ingestion of data
Articulates complex, large scale, and high impact technical design and development details to non-technical business partners
Elicits, analyzes, and understands business and data requirements to develop complete business solutions, including data models (entity relationship diagrams, dimensional data models), ETL and business rules, data life-cycle management, governance, lineage, and metadata
Ensures data is maintained in compliance with enterprise data standards, policies, and guidelines
Develops and maintains complex data models using industry standard modeling tools
Develops and maintains complex ETL jobs and frameworks using the Bank's standard tools
Provides support to the development and testing teams to resolve data issues, including escalation support on complex issues
Supports partners and stakeholders in interpreting and analyzing data
Builds effective working relationships within own pod and across partner teams to encourage collaboration on all pod deliverables

Shareholder Accountabilities

Coordinates with technology work teams such as ITS, ARE, Architecture, Enterprise Protect etc. to ensure overall delivery success

Provides oversight on post implementation activities during the warranty period
Executes & approves code check-in/ check-out into source code repository as part of source code management
Works closely with ITS/ ARE teams to support code packaging & deployment (CI & CD) into higher environments
Is the lead participant in the design & architecture reviews or the application
